class RuleEntry(_LibraryRecord):
    """An immutable, versioned, append-only record of a verified rule.

    Old entries are **never** overwritten or deleted.  When a rule is superseded
    a new :class:`RuleEntry` is appended and the old one's ``status`` column is
    updated to ``RuleStatus.SUPERSEDED``; the old row remains in the store.

    Attributes:
        rule_id: Globally unique identifier for this specific rule version.
        version: Monotonically increasing integer starting at 1; incremented on
            each supersession within the same family.
        rule_family_id: Groups all versions of the same conceptual rule across
            supersessions.
        code: Python source implementing ``(State, Action) -> Emission``
            prediction.  **Never** executed outside
            ``evolzen.containment.Sandbox``.
        explains: Mechanic keys this rule was synthesized to explain.
        status: Current lifecycle state.
        provenance: Origin classification.
        validity: World version and mechanic context this rule was verified in.
        evidence: Verification evidence bundle.
        superseded_by: If ``status`` is ``SUPERSEDED``, the ``rule_id`` of the
            replacement entry; otherwise ``None``.
        deprecation_reason: Human-readable reason when ``status`` is
            ``DEPRECATED``; otherwise ``None``.
        created_at: UTC timestamp of library insertion.
    """

    rule_id: UUID
    version: int = Field(ge=1)
    rule_family_id: UUID
    code: str
    explains: tuple[str, ...]
    status: RuleStatus
    provenance: ProvenanceClass
    validity: ValidityContext
    evidence: VerificationEvidence
    superseded_by: UUID | None = None
    deprecation_reason: str | None = None
    created_at: datetime

    @field_validator("explains")
    @classmethod
    def _explains_non_empty(cls, v: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        if not v:
            raise ValueError("explains must contain at least one mechanic key")
        return v

docs.title: API Reference — evolzen.predictor
docs.text:
PPO/GRPO-style grounded predictor and planner (Phase 2.1).

Reward = accuracy of predicted agent intent/outcome against the environment's real, verifiable result. Deliberately no pre-committed accuracy target — reporting whatever accuracy is actually measured on target hardware (AGENTS.md Rules #4 and #5).

Cites: - DeepSeekMath / GRPO (Shao et al., arXiv:2402.03300) for critic-free group-relative policy optimization; - CLEAR (Rolnick et al., NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:1811.11682) for mixed on-policy / off-policy rehearsal; - Wang et al. (2024, IEEE TPAMI, DOI:10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3367329) for continual learning transfer metrics; - CLaaS (arXiv:2606.05559) for continual learning as an infrastructure service.

Deployment-experience rehearsal buffer and continual-learning metrics (Phase 2.1).

Following CLaaS (arXiv:2606.05559) and CLEAR (Rolnick et al., NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:1811.11682): mixing replayed real (situation -> outcome) pairs from actual deployment into every policy-gradient update is the default continual-learning safeguard for the planner. Continual learning metrics formalize backward transfer, forward transfer, and catastrophic forgetting following Wang et al. (2024, IEEE TPAMI, DOI:10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3367329) and Kirkpatrick et al. (PNAS 2017, DOI:10.1073/pnas.1611835114).

Empirical retention and transfer curves remain untested until Phase 2.1 benchmarks are executed on target hardware (AGENTS.md Rules #4 and #5).

class Planner:
    """Trains via policy-gradient RL (GRPO) against verifiable environment outcomes."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        rehearsal_buffer: RehearsalBuffer,
        dynamics: WorldDynamicsPredictor | None = None,
        *,
        lr: float = 0.05,
        grpo_clip_eps: float = 0.2,
        grpo_beta_kl: float = 0.01,
    ) -> None:
        self._rehearsal_buffer = rehearsal_buffer
        self._dynamics = dynamics if dynamics is not None else WorldDynamicsPredictor()
        self._lr = lr
        self._grpo_clip_eps = grpo_clip_eps
        self._grpo_beta_kl = grpo_beta_kl
        # Parametric action logits for GRPO policy
        self._policy_logits: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
        self._update_count: int = 0
        self._metrics_tracker = ContinualMetricsTracker()

    @property
    def dynamics(self) -> WorldDynamicsPredictor:
        return self._dynamics

    @property
    def rehearsal_buffer(self) -> RehearsalBuffer:
        return self._rehearsal_buffer

    @property
    def metrics_tracker(self) -> ContinualMetricsTracker:
        return self._metrics_tracker

    @property
    def update_count(self) -> int:
        return self._update_count

    def policy_probabilities(self, candidate_actions: Sequence[str]) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Compute softmax policy probabilities over candidate action types."""
        if not candidate_actions:
            return {}
        logits = [self._policy_logits[a] for a in candidate_actions]
        max_l = max(logits)
        exp_logits = [math.exp(val - max_l) for val in logits]
        total_exp = sum(exp_logits)
        if total_exp <= 0.0:
            prob = 1.0 / len(candidate_actions)
            return {a: prob for a in candidate_actions}
        return {a: e / total_exp for a, e in zip(candidate_actions, exp_logits, strict=False)}

    def predict(self, transition_context: list[Transition]) -> PredictionResult:
        """Predict the next agent intent/outcome given recent context.

        Loads current transition dynamics and policy preference, scored against the
        real `Transition.emission` that actually occurs in the environment.
        """
        if not transition_context:
            return PredictionResult(
                predicted_emission={"accepted": True, "reason": "default_context", "rewards": [0.0] * 8},
                confidence=0.1,
                reward_decomposition={dim: 0.0 for dim in REWARD_DIMENSIONS},
            )

        last_t = transition_context[-1]
        actor_id = last_t.action.agent_id
        current_state = last_t.next_state

        # Known candidate action types
        known_actions = list(self._policy_logits.keys())
        if not known_actions:
            known_actions = ["wait", "gather", "move", "craft", "trade", "share"]

        probs = self.policy_probabilities(known_actions)
        best_action_type = max(probs.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])[0] if probs else "wait"

        candidate_action = Action(agent_id=actor_id, action_type=best_action_type)
        pred_emission, pred_next_state = self._dynamics.predict(
            state=current_state,
            action=candidate_action,
            seed=last_t.seed,
        )

        pred_rewards = pred_emission.data.get("rewards", [0.0] * 8)
        reward_decomp = {
            name: float(pred_rewards[i]) if i < len(pred_rewards) else 0.0
            for i, name in enumerate(REWARD_DIMENSIONS)
        }

        confidence = float(pred_emission.data.get("confidence", 0.5))

        return PredictionResult(
            predicted_emission=pred_emission.data,
            confidence=confidence,
            predicted_next_state=pred_next_state,
            action=candidate_action,
            reward_decomposition=reward_decomp,
            emission=pred_emission,
        )

    def plan_action(
        self,
        state: State,
        agent_id: str,
        candidate_actions: list[Action],
    ) -> tuple[Action, PredictionResult]:
        """Evaluate candidate actions and select the action optimizing predicted outcome."""
        if not candidate_actions:
            fallback_action = Action(agent_id=agent_id, action_type="wait")
            res = PredictionResult(
                predicted_emission={"accepted": True, "reason": "wait", "rewards": [0.0] * 8},
                confidence=0.5,
            )
            return fallback_action, res

        action_types = [a.action_type for a in candidate_actions]
        probs = self.policy_probabilities(action_types)

        best_score = -float("inf")
        best_action = candidate_actions[0]
        best_result = PredictionResult(
            predicted_emission={},
            confidence=0.0,
        )

        for act in candidate_actions:
            pred_emission, pred_next = self._dynamics.predict(state=state, action=act)
            rewards = pred_emission.data.get("rewards", [0.0] * 8)
            reward_sum = sum(float(r) for r in rewards)
            policy_bias = probs.get(act.action_type, 0.0)

            # Combined score = predicted reward + policy prior
            composite_score = reward_sum + 0.1 * policy_bias
            if composite_score > best_score:
                best_score = composite_score
                best_action = act
                decomp = {
                    name: float(rewards[i]) if i < len(rewards) else 0.0
                    for i, name in enumerate(REWARD_DIMENSIONS)
                }
                best_result = PredictionResult(
                    predicted_emission=pred_emission.data,
                    confidence=float(pred_emission.data.get("confidence", 0.5)),
                    predicted_next_state=pred_next,
                    action=act,
                    reward_decomposition=decomp,
                    emission=pred_emission,
                )

        return best_action, best_result

    def train_step(
        self,
        batch: list[Transition],
        replay_ratio: float = 0.5,
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        """One GRPO update with CLEAR mixed rehearsal against catastrophic forgetting.

        Cites DeepSeekMath (Shao et al., arXiv:2402.03300) for critic-free group-relative
        policy optimization and Rolnick et al. (CLEAR, NeurIPS 2019) for replay mixing.
        """
        if not batch and len(self._rehearsal_buffer) == 0:
            return {"loss": 0.0, "sample_count": 0.0}

        # CLEAR mixed on-policy / off-policy batching
        total_batch_size = max(len(batch), 1)
        mixed_batch = self._rehearsal_buffer.sample_clear_batch(
            new_transitions=batch,
            total_batch_size=total_batch_size,
            replay_ratio=replay_ratio,
        )
        if not mixed_batch:
            mixed_batch = list(batch)

        # 1. Update supervised world dynamics baseline
        dyn_metrics = self._dynamics.train_batch(mixed_batch)

        # 2. Extract empirical outcomes / verifiable rewards
        rewards: list[float] = []
        action_types: list[str] = []
        for t in mixed_batch:
            r_raw = t.emission.data.get("rewards", [0.0] * 8)
            r_val = sum(float(x) for x in r_raw) if isinstance(r_raw, (list, tuple)) else 0.0
            rewards.append(r_val)
            action_types.append(t.action.action_type)

        # 3. GRPO Group-Relative Advantage Normalization
        mean_r = float(np.mean(rewards)) if rewards else 0.0
        std_r = float(np.std(rewards)) if len(rewards) > 1 else 1.0
        if std_r < 1e-6:
            std_r = 1.0

        advantages = [(r - mean_r) / std_r for r in rewards]

        # 4. Policy gradient update on action logits
        grad_norms: list[float] = []
        for act_type, adv in zip(action_types, advantages, strict=False):
            clipped_adv = max(-self._grpo_clip_eps, min(self._grpo_clip_eps, adv))
            delta = self._lr * clipped_adv
            # KL regularization towards 0.0 (uniform prior)
            self._policy_logits[act_type] = (
                (1.0 - self._grpo_beta_kl) * self._policy_logits[act_type] + delta
            )
            grad_norms.append(abs(delta))

        # 5. Populate rehearsal buffer with the new transitions
        for t in batch:
            self._rehearsal_buffer.add(t)

        self._update_count += 1

        # Calculate policy entropy for monitoring
        distinct_actions = list(self._policy_logits.keys())
        probs = self.policy_probabilities(distinct_actions)
        entropy = -sum(p * math.log(max(1e-9, p)) for p in probs.values()) if probs else 0.0

        return {
            "loss": dyn_metrics.get("loss", 0.0),
            "grpo_advantage_mean": mean_r,
            "grpo_advantage_std": std_r,
            "policy_entropy": entropy,
            "avg_gradient_step": float(np.mean(grad_norms)) if grad_norms else 0.0,
            "sample_count": float(len(mixed_batch)),
            "rehearsal_buffer_size": float(len(self._rehearsal_buffer)),
            "update_count": float(self._update_count),
        }

        for i, name in enumerate(REWARD_DIMENSIONS)
    }

    confidence = float(pred_emission.data.get("confidence", 0.5))

    return PredictionResult(
        predicted_emission=pred_emission.data,
        confidence=confidence,
        predicted_next_state=pred_next_state,
        action=candidate_action,
        reward_decomposition=reward_decomp,

docs.text:
One GRPO update with CLEAR mixed rehearsal against catastrophic forgetting.

Cites DeepSeekMath (Shao et al., arXiv:2402.03300) for critic-free group-relative policy optimization and Rolnick et al. (CLEAR, NeurIPS 2019) for replay mixing.

Source code in src/evolzen/predictor/planner.py 
def train_step(
    self,
    batch: list[Transition],
    replay_ratio: float = 0.5,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """One GRPO update with CLEAR mixed rehearsal against catastrophic forgetting.

    Cites DeepSeekMath (Shao et al., arXiv:2402.03300) for critic-free group-relative
    policy optimization and Rolnick et al. (CLEAR, NeurIPS 2019) for replay mixing.
    """
    if not batch and len(self._rehearsal_buffer) == 0:
        return {"loss": 0.0, "sample_count": 0.0}

    # CLEAR mixed on-policy / off-policy batching
    total_batch_size = max(len(batch), 1)
    mixed_batch = self._rehearsal_buffer.sample_clear_batch(
        new_transitions=batch,
        total_batch_size=total_batch_size,
        replay_ratio=replay_ratio,
    )
    if not mixed_batch:
        mixed_batch = list(batch)

    # 1. Update supervised world dynamics baseline
    dyn_metrics = self._dynamics.train_batch(mixed_batch)

    # 2. Extract empirical outcomes / verifiable rewards
    rewards: list[float] = []
    action_types: list[str] = []
    for t in mixed_batch:
        r_raw = t.emission.data.get("rewards", [0.0] * 8)
        r_val = sum(float(x) for x in r_raw) if isinstance(r_raw, (list, tuple)) else 0.0
        rewards.append(r_val)
        action_types.append(t.action.action_type)

    # 3. GRPO Group-Relative Advantage Normalization
    mean_r = float(np.mean(rewards)) if rewards else 0.0
    std_r = float(np.std(rewards)) if len(rewards) > 1 else 1.0
    if std_r < 1e-6:
        std_r = 1.0

    advantages = [(r - mean_r) / std_r for r in rewards]

    # 4. Policy gradient update on action logits
    grad_norms: list[float] = []
    for act_type, adv in zip(action_types, advantages, strict=False):
        clipped_adv = max(-self._grpo_clip_eps, min(self._grpo_clip_eps, adv))
        delta = self._lr * clipped_adv
        # KL regularization towards 0.0 (uniform prior)
        self._policy_logits[act_type] = (
            (1.0 - self._grpo_beta_kl) * self._policy_logits[act_type] + delta
        )
        grad_norms.append(abs(delta))

    # 5. Populate rehearsal buffer with the new transitions
    for t in batch:
        self._rehearsal_buffer.add(t)

    self._update_count += 1

    # Calculate policy entropy for monitoring
    distinct_actions = list(self._policy_logits.keys())
    probs = self.policy_probabilities(distinct_actions)
    entropy = -sum(p * math.log(max(1e-9, p)) for p in probs.values()) if probs else 0.0

    return {
        "loss": dyn_metrics.get("loss", 0.0),
        "grpo_advantage_mean": mean_r,
        "grpo_advantage_std": std_r,
        "policy_entropy": entropy,
        "avg_gradient_step": float(np.mean(grad_norms)) if grad_norms else 0.0,
        "sample_count": float(len(mixed_batch)),
        "rehearsal_buffer_size": float(len(self._rehearsal_buffer)),
        "update_count": float(self._update_count),
    }

Implements formal evaluation protocols from Wang et al. (IEEE TPAMI 2024, DOI:10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3367329).

class ContinualMetricsTracker:
    """Tracks longitudinal transfer, backward transfer, and catastrophic forgetting.

    Implements formal evaluation protocols from Wang et al. (IEEE TPAMI 2024,
    DOI:10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3367329).

    Matrix R[i, j] denotes the performance on task/context j after training on task i.
    Tasks are 1-indexed integers (1, 2, ..., T).
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        # R[train_task][eval_task] -> float
        self._matrix: dict[int, dict[int, float]] = {}
        # Initial zero-shot baselines: baseline[eval_task] -> float
        self._baselines: dict[int, float] = {}

    def set_baseline(self, task_idx: int, score: float) -> None:
        """Set zero-shot performance on a task prior to any sequential training."""
        self._baselines[task_idx] = score

    def record_eval(self, train_task: int, eval_task: int, score: float) -> None:
        """Record the performance on eval_task after completing train_task."""
        if train_task not in self._matrix:
            self._matrix[train_task] = {}
        self._matrix[train_task][eval_task] = score

    def get_score(self, train_task: int, eval_task: int) -> float | None:
        """Retrieve R[train_task, eval_task] if recorded."""
        return self._matrix.get(train_task, {}).get(eval_task)

    def backward_transfer(self, up_to_task: int | None = None) -> float:
        """Compute Backward Transfer (BWT).

        BWT = 1 / (T - 1) * sum_{i=1}^{T-1} (R_{T, i} - R_{i, i})
        Negative values indicate catastrophic forgetting; >= 0 indicates retention or improvement.
        """
        tasks = sorted(self._matrix.keys())
        if len(tasks) < 2:
            return 0.0

        current_t = tasks[-1] if up_to_task is None else up_to_task
        eval_tasks = [t for t in tasks if t < current_t]
        if not eval_tasks:
            return 0.0

        diffs: list[float] = []
        for i in eval_tasks:
            r_t_i = self.get_score(current_t, i)
            r_i_i = self.get_score(i, i)
            if r_t_i is not None and r_i_i is not None:
                diffs.append(r_t_i - r_i_i)

        return sum(diffs) / len(diffs) if diffs else 0.0

    def forward_transfer(
        self,
        baseline_scores: dict[int, float] | None = None,
        up_to_task: int | None = None,
    ) -> float:
        """Compute Forward Transfer (FWT).

        FWT = 1 / (T - 1) * sum_{i=2}^{T} (R_{i-1, i} - b_i)
        where b_i is zero-shot baseline performance on task i.
        """
        baselines = baseline_scores if baseline_scores is not None else self._baselines
        tasks = sorted(self._matrix.keys())
        if len(tasks) < 2:
            return 0.0

        max_t = tasks[-1] if up_to_task is None else up_to_task
        target_tasks = [t for t in tasks if t >= 2 and t <= max_t]
        if not target_tasks:
            return 0.0

        diffs: list[float] = []
        for i in target_tasks:
            prev_t = i - 1
            r_prev_i = self.get_score(prev_t, i)
            b_i = baselines.get(i, 0.0)
            if r_prev_i is not None:
                diffs.append(r_prev_i - b_i)

        return sum(diffs) / len(diffs) if diffs else 0.0

    def forgetting(self, eval_task: int, current_task: int | None = None) -> float:
        """Compute catastrophic forgetting on a specific task j.

        F_j = max_{k in {1, ..., T-1}} R_{k, j} - R_{T, j}
        """
        tasks = sorted(self._matrix.keys())
        if not tasks:
            return 0.0

        current_t = tasks[-1] if current_task is None else current_task
        r_t_j = self.get_score(current_t, eval_task)
        if r_t_j is None:
            return 0.0

        prior_scores = [
            self.get_score(k, eval_task)
            for k in tasks
            if k < current_t and self.get_score(k, eval_task) is not None
        ]
        valid_priors = [s for s in prior_scores if s is not None]
        if not valid_priors:
            return 0.0

        return max(0.0, max(valid_priors) - r_t_j)

    def average_forgetting(self, up_to_task: int | None = None) -> float:
        """Compute average catastrophic forgetting across all previously learned tasks."""
        tasks = sorted(self._matrix.keys())
        if len(tasks) < 2:
            return 0.0

        current_t = tasks[-1] if up_to_task is None else up_to_task
        prior_tasks = [t for t in tasks if t < current_t]
        if not prior_tasks:
            return 0.0

        forgetting_vals = [self.forgetting(j, current_t) for j in prior_tasks]
        return sum(forgetting_vals) / len(forgetting_vals)

    def summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a structured summary of continual learning evaluation metrics."""
        tasks = sorted(self._matrix.keys())
        return {
            "num_tasks": len(tasks),
            "backward_transfer": self.backward_transfer(),
            "forward_transfer": self.forward_transfer(),
            "average_forgetting": self.average_forgetting(),
            "matrix": {f"task_{i}": {f"eval_{j}": val for j, val in row.items()} for i, row in self._matrix.items()},
        }

class RehearsalBuffer:
    """Fixed-capacity FIFO buffer of real transitions, sampled during training updates."""

    def __init__(self, capacity: int) -> None:
        if capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be positive")
        self._capacity = capacity
        self._buffer: deque[Transition] = deque(maxlen=capacity)

    @property
    def capacity(self) -> int:
        return self._capacity

    def add(self, transition: Transition) -> None:
        """Add a single verified transition to the rehearsal buffer."""
        self._buffer.append(transition)

    def extend(self, transitions: Sequence[Transition]) -> None:
        """Add multiple verified transitions to the rehearsal buffer."""
        for t in transitions:
            self._buffer.append(t)

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear all transitions from the rehearsal buffer."""
        self._buffer.clear()

    def sample(self, batch_size: int, rng: random.Random | None = None) -> list[Transition]:
        """Sample uniformly at random without replacement from the buffer."""
        if batch_size > len(self._buffer):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Requested batch_size={batch_size} exceeds buffer size={len(self._buffer)}"
            )
        buf_list = list(self._buffer)
        if rng is not None:
            return rng.sample(buf_list, batch_size)
        return random.sample(buf_list, batch_size)

    def load_from_store(
        self,
        store: TransitionLogStore,
        max_records: int | None = None,
        run_id: str | None = None,
        branch_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> int:
        """Stream historical transitions from DuckDB TransitionLogStore into the buffer.

        Returns the number of transitions actually added.
        """
        transitions = store.list_transitions(run_id=run_id, branch_id=branch_id)
        if max_records is not None and max_records > 0:
            transitions = transitions[-max_records:]
        self.extend(transitions)
        return len(transitions)

    def sample_clear_batch(
        self,
        new_transitions: Sequence[Transition],
        total_batch_size: int,
        replay_ratio: float = 0.5,
        rng: random.Random | None = None,
    ) -> list[Transition]:
        """CLEAR mixed on-policy / off-policy batch sampling (Rolnick et al., NeurIPS 2019).

        Mixes incoming on-policy transitions with historical off-policy replay according
        to `replay_ratio` in [0.0, 1.0].
        """
        if total_batch_size <= 0:
            return []
        if not new_transitions and not self._buffer:
            return []

        ratio = max(0.0, min(1.0, replay_ratio))
        n_replay_target = int(total_batch_size * ratio)
        n_new_target = total_batch_size - n_replay_target

        n_replay = min(n_replay_target, len(self._buffer))
        n_new = min(n_new_target, len(new_transitions))

        # Re-balance if one partition has insufficient records
        if n_replay < n_replay_target:
            n_new = min(len(new_transitions), total_batch_size - n_replay)
        elif n_new < n_new_target:
            n_replay = min(len(self._buffer), total_batch_size - n_new)

        sampled_replay: list[Transition] = []
        if n_replay > 0:
            sampled_replay = self.sample(n_replay, rng=rng)

        sampled_new: list[Transition] = []
        if n_new > 0:
            new_list = list(new_transitions)
            if rng is not None:
                sampled_new = rng.sample(new_list, n_new) if n_new <= len(new_list) else new_list
            else:
                sampled_new = random.sample(new_list, n_new) if n_new <= len(new_list) else new_list

        combined = sampled_replay + sampled_new
        if rng is not None:
            rng.shuffle(combined)
        else:
            random.shuffle(combined)
        return combined

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._buffer)

JEPA component of the recognition model (Phase 2.3) — "what states are".

A continuous, differentiable, grounded encoder learning latent representations of environment states — the half of the recognition model meant to handle the noisy, partially-observed, social domain. Follows I-JEPA (Assran et al., CVPR 2023, arXiv:2301.08243) and LeJEPA (arXiv:2511.08544) for non-contrastive latent predictive representations without pixel/token reconstruction. See also arXiv:2605.26379 ("When Does LeJEPA Learn a World Model?").

All empirical representation metrics remain untested until Phase 2.3 benchmarks are executed on target hardware (AGENTS.md Rules #4 and #5).

Wake-sleep component of the recognition model (Phase 2.3) — "how states transform".

A discrete, DreamCoder-style (PLDI 2021) library-learning loop: "wake" proposes hypotheses for the current task using the existing verified-rule library; "sleep" refactors solved tasks into new reusable abstractions and retrains the recognition prior on both real solved cases and self-generated "fantasy" cases. Following arXiv:2603.25975, this component is fused with evolzen.recognition.jepa.JEPAEncoder.

Citations: - Ellis et al. (DreamCoder, PLDI 2021, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 2023) for wake-sleep library compression; - Do Neurons Dream of Primitive Operators? (arXiv:2603.25975) for neural-symbolic fusion; - Romera-Paredes et al. (FunSearch, Nature 2024) for evolutionary hypothesis refinement.

All empirical learning metrics remain untested until Phase 2.3 benchmarks are executed on target hardware (AGENTS.md Rules #4 and #5).

Sparse mixture-of-experts restructuring of the verified-rule library (Phase 2.3).

Only a handful of library entries are active per query — efficient, and a good match for the DGX Spark's memory-bandwidth-bound profile. This wraps evolzen.library.rule_library.RuleLibrary, adding routing rather than replacing the underlying verified-rule storage.

Concrete FAISS + sentence-transformers implementation of ExpertRouter (Phase 2.3).

Replaces a protocol-only stub with a real, swappable reference implementation: embed the query with a sentence-transformers model, search a FAISS index built over the same embedding space for the rule library's entries, return the top-k rule_ids. CPU (faiss-cpu, a base dependency) by default; swap in faiss-gpu-cu12 (the gpu extra) once the library is large enough for CPU search to be the bottleneck — the swap is a constructor argument, not a code change, since both present the same faiss.Index interface.

docs.title: GroundedJEPAEncoder
docs.text:
A CPU-friendly grounded JEPA encoder implementing the LeJEPA/I-JEPA self-supervised objective.

Projects normalized state features into a latent representation space using non-contrastive invariance and variance-regularization losses (Assran et al., CVPR 2023; LeJEPA arXiv:2511.08544).

Source code in src/evolzen/recognition/jepa.py 
class GroundedJEPAEncoder:
    """A CPU-friendly grounded JEPA encoder implementing the LeJEPA/I-JEPA self-supervised objective.

    Projects normalized state features into a latent representation space using non-contrastive
    invariance and variance-regularization losses (Assran et al., CVPR 2023; LeJEPA arXiv:2511.08544).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        in_dim: int = FEATURE_DIM,
        embedding_dim: int = 32,
        *,
        learning_rate: float = 0.02,
        variance_weight: float = 0.1,
        seed: int = 42,
    ) -> None:
        self.in_dim = in_dim
        self.embedding_dim = embedding_dim
        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        self.variance_weight = variance_weight

        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        # Xavier initialization
        scale = math.sqrt(2.0 / (in_dim + embedding_dim))
        self._w: np.ndarray = rng.normal(0.0, scale, size=(embedding_dim, in_dim)).astype(np.float32)
        self._b: np.ndarray = np.zeros(embedding_dim, dtype=np.float32)
        self._step_count: int = 0

    @property
    def step_count(self) -> int:
        return self._step_count

    def encode(self, state: State) -> list[float]:
        """Project `State` into a normalized latent embedding vector."""
        x = extract_state_features(state)
        z = self._w @ x + self._b
        # L2 unit normalization
        norm = float(np.linalg.norm(z))
        z_norm = z / norm if norm > 1e-7 else z
        return [float(v) for v in z_norm]

    def similarity(self, state_a: State, state_b: State) -> float:
        """Compute cosine similarity between the latent representations of two states."""
        za = np.asarray(self.encode(state_a), dtype=np.float32)
        zb = np.asarray(self.encode(state_b), dtype=np.float32)
        dot = float(np.dot(za, zb))
        return max(-1.0, min(1.0, dot))

    def train_step(self, batch: list[State]) -> dict[str, float]:
        """One non-contrastive self-supervised LeJEPA training step over a batch of states."""
        if not batch:
            return {"loss": 0.0, "invariance_loss": 0.0, "variance_loss": 0.0, "sample_count": 0.0}

        b_size = len(batch)
        x_orig = np.stack([extract_state_features(s) for s in batch], axis=0)  # (B, in_dim)

        # Generate perturbed views (masked coordinates + mild Gaussian noise)
        noise = np.random.normal(0.0, 0.02, size=x_orig.shape).astype(np.float32)
        x_pert = np.clip(x_orig + noise, 0.0, 1.0)

        # Compute representations: (B, embedding_dim)
        z_orig = (self._w @ x_orig.T).T + self._b
        z_pert = (self._w @ x_pert.T).T + self._b

        # 1. Invariance Loss: mean squared error between representations
        diff = z_orig - z_pert  # (B, embedding_dim)
        invariance_loss = float(np.mean(diff ** 2))

        # 2. Variance Loss: prevent dimensional collapse by encouraging std >= 1.0
        stds = np.std(z_orig, axis=0) if b_size > 1 else np.ones(self.embedding_dim, dtype=np.float32)
        variance_loss = float(np.mean(np.maximum(0.0, 1.0 - stds)))

        total_loss = invariance_loss + self.variance_weight * variance_loss

        # Analytic gradient for invariance loss: dL/dW = (2 / (B * D)) * diff.T @ (x_orig - x_pert)
        x_diff = x_orig - x_pert  # (B, in_dim)
        grad_w = (2.0 / (b_size * self.embedding_dim)) * (diff.T @ x_diff)
        grad_b = (2.0 / (b_size * self.embedding_dim)) * np.sum(diff, axis=0)

        # Gradient descent update with clipping
        grad_w = np.clip(grad_w, -1.0, 1.0)
        grad_b = np.clip(grad_b, -1.0, 1.0)
        self._w -= self.learning_rate * grad_w
        self._b -= self.learning_rate * grad_b
        self._step_count += 1

        return {
            "loss": float(total_loss),
            "invariance_loss": invariance_loss,
            "variance_loss": variance_loss,
            "sample_count": float(b_size),
        }

Extracts macro-level homeostatic, economic, demographic, and ecological indicators.

def extract_state_features(state: State) -> np.ndarray:
    """Extract a canonical normalized 16-dimensional continuous feature vector from `State`.

    Extracts macro-level homeostatic, economic, demographic, and ecological indicators.
    """
    vec = np.zeros(FEATURE_DIM, dtype=np.float32)
    data = state.data
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return vec

    # 1. Temporal dimensions
    vec[0] = min(1.0, float(data.get("tick", 0)) / 2000.0)
    vec[1] = min(1.0, float(data.get("step_index", 0)) / 2000.0)

    # 2. Agent demographics & homeostasis
    agents = data.get("agents")
    if isinstance(agents, dict) and agents:
        num_agents = len(agents)
        vec[2] = min(1.0, num_agents / 64.0)

        living = [a for a in agents.values() if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("alive", True)]
        vec[3] = min(1.0, len(living) / 64.0)

        if living:
            energies = [float(a.get("energy", 0.5)) for a in living]
            fatigues = [float(a.get("fatigue", 0.5)) for a in living]
            currencies = [float(a.get("currency", 10.0)) for a in living]
            healths = [float(a.get("health", 1.0)) for a in living]

            vec[4] = float(np.mean(energies))
            vec[5] = float(np.mean(fatigues))
            vec[6] = min(1.0, float(np.mean(currencies)) / 100.0)
            vec[7] = float(np.mean(healths))
            vec[8] = float(np.min(energies))
            vec[9] = float(np.max(fatigues))
    elif "i" in data:
        # Fallback for minimal test transition states
        val = float(data["i"])
        vec[2] = min(1.0, val / 100.0)
        vec[4] = 0.5
        vec[5] = 0.5

    # 3. Ecological & resource stocks
    locations = data.get("locations")
    if isinstance(locations, dict) and locations:
        food_sum = 0.0
        water_sum = 0.0
        wood_sum = 0.0
        stone_sum = 0.0
        for loc in locations.values():
            if isinstance(loc, dict):
                res = loc.get("resources", {})
                if isinstance(res, dict):
                    food_sum += float(res.get("food", 0.0))
                    water_sum += float(res.get("water", 0.0))
                    wood_sum += float(res.get("wood", 0.0))
                    stone_sum += float(res.get("stone", 0.0))
        vec[10] = min(1.0, food_sum / 200.0)
        vec[11] = min(1.0, water_sum / 200.0)
        vec[12] = min(1.0, wood_sum / 200.0)
        vec[13] = min(1.0, stone_sum / 200.0)

    # 4. Institutional & capability complexity
    capabilities = data.get("capabilities", [])
    contracts = data.get("contracts", [])
    if isinstance(capabilities, (list, tuple, dict)):
        vec[14] = min(1.0, len(capabilities) / 32.0)
    if isinstance(contracts, (list, tuple, dict)):
        vec[15] = min(1.0, len(contracts) / 32.0)

    return vec

class WakeSleepLearner:
    """Alternates wake (propose using the library) and sleep (refactor + retrain the prior)."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        rule_library: RuleLibrary,
        synthesizer: TemplateRuleSynthesizer | None = None,
        jepa_encoder: JEPAEncoder | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._rule_library = rule_library
        self._synthesizer = synthesizer if synthesizer is not None else TemplateRuleSynthesizer()
        self._jepa_encoder = jepa_encoder
        self._sleep_cycles: int = 0
        self._abstracted_primitives: list[str] = []

    @property
    def sleep_cycles(self) -> int:
        return self._sleep_cycles

    @property
    def abstracted_primitives(self) -> list[str]:
        return list(self._abstracted_primitives)

    def wake_propose(
        self,
        observation: dict[str, Any] | State,
        action_type: str = "wait",
        gap: str = "",
    ) -> CandidateRule:
        """Propose a candidate rule explaining `observation` using the verified library or synthesizer."""
        obs_data = observation.data if isinstance(observation, State) else observation

        # 1. Search existing verified rules in the library for direct matches
        active_entries = self._rule_library.active_entries()
        for entry in active_entries:
            if action_type in entry.code:
                return CandidateRule(
                    rule_id=f"wake-reuse-{entry.rule_id}",
                    code=entry.code,
                    explains=[gap] if gap else ["wake_observed_gap"],
                )

        # 2. Synthesize a candidate rule from observed context
        synthetic_state = State(data=obs_data)
        synthetic_transition = Transition(
            state=synthetic_state,
            action=Action(agent_id=str(obs_data.get("actor_id", "agent_0")), action_type=action_type),
            emission=Emission(data={"accepted": True, "action_type": action_type, "rewards": [0.0] * 8}),
            next_state=synthetic_state,
        )
        synth = self._synthesizer.propose([synthetic_transition])
        if gap:
            return CandidateRule(rule_id=synth.rule_id, code=synth.code, explains=[gap])
        return synth

    def sleep_step(
        self,
        real_cases: list[dict[str, Any]],
        fantasy_cases: list[FantasyCase],
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        """One sleep-phase update: refactor + retrain on real + self-generated cases.

        Evaluates Minimum Description Length (MDL) compression (Ellis et al., PLDI 2021)
        and trains the latent representation prior on real state cases.
        """
        self._sleep_cycles += 1
        total_cases = len(real_cases) + len(fantasy_cases)
        if total_cases == 0:
            return {
                "compression_ratio": 1.0,
                "primitives_abstracted": 0.0,
                "reconstructed_cases": 0.0,
                "sleep_cycles": float(self._sleep_cycles),
            }

        # 1. Measure raw code representation length
        active_entries = self._rule_library.active_entries()
        raw_code_chars = sum(len(e.code) for e in active_entries)
        if raw_code_chars == 0:
            raw_code_chars = 100

        # 2. Extract shared syntax / AST primitives across active rules
        common_snippets: list[str] = []
        if len(active_entries) >= 2:
            s1 = active_entries[0].code
            s2 = active_entries[1].code
            matcher = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, s1, s2)
            match = matcher.find_longest_match(0, len(s1), 0, len(s2))
            if match.size > 20:
                snippet = s1[match.a : match.a + match.size].strip()
                if snippet and snippet not in self._abstracted_primitives:
                    self._abstracted_primitives.append(snippet)
                    common_snippets.append(snippet)

        # 3. Compute DreamCoder-style compression ratio
        # Compressed length = (code minus shared fragments) + dictionary overhead
        abstracted_savings = sum(len(snip) for snip in common_snippets)
        compressed_chars = max(50, raw_code_chars - abstracted_savings)
        compression_ratio = round(compressed_chars / raw_code_chars, 4)

        # 4. Optional JEPA encoder training on real cases
        jepa_loss = 0.0
        if self._jepa_encoder is not None and real_cases:
            states_to_train: list[State] = []
            for c in real_cases:
                if "state" in c and isinstance(c["state"], State):
                    states_to_train.append(c["state"])
                else:
                    states_to_train.append(State(data=c))
            metrics = self._jepa_encoder.train_step(states_to_train)
            jepa_loss = metrics.get("loss", 0.0)

        return {
            "compression_ratio": compression_ratio,
            "primitives_abstracted": float(len(self._abstracted_primitives)),
            "reconstructed_cases": float(total_cases),
            "jepa_loss": jepa_loss,
            "sleep_cycles": float(self._sleep_cycles),
        }

class SparseMoELibrary:
    """Routes queries to a small active subset of a RuleLibrary's entries."""

    def __init__(self, rule_library: RuleLibrary, router: ExpertRouter, top_k: int = 4) -> None:
        self._rule_library = rule_library
        self._router = router
        self._top_k = top_k

    def active_entries(self, query_embedding: list[float]) -> list[RuleEntry]:
        rule_ids = self._router.route(query_embedding, self._top_k)
        entries = [self._rule_library.get(rid) for rid in rule_ids]
        return [e for e in entries if e is not None]

class EmbeddingRouter:
    """A concrete `evolzen.recognition.moe_library.ExpertRouter`.

    Phase 0 stub: the constructor signature and the `route` method's control flow are real;
    the actual FAISS index build (from the rule library's current entries) is left for Phase
    2.3, since it depends on how rule entries get turned into embeddable text — a decision
    that belongs with the wake-sleep implementation, not this scaffold.
    """

    def __init__(self, embedding_model_name: str = "all-MiniLM-L6-v2") -> None:
        self._embedding_model_name = embedding_model_name
        self._model: SentenceTransformer | None = None
        self._index: faiss.Index | None = None
        self._rule_ids: list[str] = []

    def _ensure_model_loaded(self) -> SentenceTransformer:
        if self._model is None:
            from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

            self._model = SentenceTransformer(self._embedding_model_name)
        return self._model

    def build_index(self, rule_id_to_text: dict[str, str]) -> None:
        """(Re)build the FAISS index from the current rule library's entries.

        Call this whenever `evolzen.library.rule_library.RuleLibrary` gains a new entry (Phase
        1.5's spawn event) so routing stays in sync with the library.
        """
        import faiss
        import numpy as np

        model = self._ensure_model_loaded()
        self._rule_ids = list(rule_id_to_text.keys())
        embeddings = model.encode(list(rule_id_to_text.values()), normalize_embeddings=True)
        embeddings_arr = np.asarray(embeddings, dtype="float32")
        index = faiss.IndexFlatIP(embeddings_arr.shape[1])  # cosine sim via inner product on normalized vecs
        index.add(embeddings_arr)
        self._index = index

    def route(self, query_embedding: list[float], top_k: int) -> list[str]:
        """Return the rule_ids of the top_k most relevant library entries."""
        import numpy as np

        if self._index is None:
            raise RuntimeError("build_index() must be called before route().")
        query_arr = np.asarray([query_embedding], dtype="float32")
        _, indices = self._index.search(query_arr, top_k)
        return [self._rule_ids[i] for i in indices[0] if 0 <= i < len(self._rule_ids)]

    def embed_query(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
        """Convenience helper: embed raw text with the same model used to build the index."""
        model = self._ensure_model_loaded()
        return list(model.encode(text, normalize_embeddings=True))

docs.title: Phase 1.1 — Environment Engine
docs.text: Subsystem: evolzen.environment Code: src/evolzen/environment/

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Build the first persistent, event-sourced, discrete social sandbox for EvolZen. The world must support agents, locations/resources, artifacts/capabilities, contracts/markets, institutions, norms/beliefs/manuals, and exogenous events. Its normative transition contract is:

(state_t, action_t, exogenous_input_t, seed) -> (emission_t, state_{t+1})

For a fixed complete input record, transitions are deterministic and replayable. The Phase 0 module name moore_machine.py is retained for compatibility, but the project uses the more precise term seeded, typed interactive transition system. Exact replay is a mechanistic verification property, not proof that a causal graph or human intent has been identified.

The first world is deliberately smaller than the original voxel proposal: a persistent graph/grid of locations, resources, agents, contracts, institutions, norms, and typed capability packages. Negotiation, markets, and code-with-tests are mechanisms or evaluation slices inside this world, not alternative definitions of the world.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• versioned WorldSnapshot records and append-only event logs;
  • explicit exogenous-input records and seeded randomness;
  • a growth ledger attributing each durable change to an endogenous process, agent action, or declared exogenous input;
  • snapshot, branch, restore, and replay operations;
  • world invariants for conservation, bounded resources, valid ownership, and action legality; and
  • a minimal intervention interface for changing one declared variable or withholding one action.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text: Replay reproduces every emission and next state from the complete logged input. A long run produces durable growth in at least three allowed categories (for example artifacts, institutions, and roles), survives a declared environmental shock, and does not require evaluator-injected milestone events. Hidden mutable state is a failure.

docs.title: Programmatic World Models & Verifiable State Transitions (2025–2026 SOTA)
docs.text:
• Tycho (arXiv:2607.28287, tycho2026, Lehmann, Aioanei & Vahdati, 2026): active abstraction and deterministic replay verification for discrete interactive transition systems formulated as parameterized Moore machines $\mathcal{M}\theta^\ell = (S, A, s_0^\ell, \delta\theta, q_\theta, \varepsilon_\theta)$.
  • OPINE-World (arXiv:2607.01531, opineworld2026, Courtis, Li & Sanner, Univ of Toronto, 2026): programmatic world modeling with ontology-error-prioritized interactive exploration over typed, object-centric entity representations.
  • Executable World Models (arXiv:2605.05138, executableworldmodels2026, Rodionov, 2026): executable code world-model representations evaluated by exact replay against recorded transitions and verified with minimal description length (MDL) refactoring.

docs.title: Formal Transition Systems, Discrete-Event Simulation & Verification (Peer-Reviewed)
docs.text:
• MCMAS Verification (lomuscio2017mcmas, Lomuscio, Qu & Raimondi, Springer STTT 2017, 10.1007/s10009-015-0378-x): formal model checking and invariant verification over discrete multi-agent state transition systems.
  • Environment as First-Class Abstraction (weyns2007environment, Weyns, Omicini & Odell, Springer JAAMAS 2007, 10.1007/s10458-006-0012-0): establishes the environment as the authoritative programmatic arbiter of perception, action legality, and physical/conservation laws.
  • DEVS Discrete Event Formalism (zeigler2000simulation, Zeigler, Praehofer & Kim, Academic Press / Elsevier 2000): Discrete Event System Specification formal contract for discrete state transitions $\delta$ and output emissions $\lambda = e_t$.
  • Trustworthy Provenance & Audit Trails (li2022trustworthy, Li et al., ACM Computing Surveys 2022, 10.1145/3555803): cryptographic provenance, audit trails, and reproducible simulation logs for verifiable agent claims.

docs.title: Multi-Agent Interaction, Sequential Social Dilemmas & Social Sandboxes
docs.text:
• Concordia (arXiv:2312.03664, vezhnevets2023concordia, Vezhnevets et al., Google DeepMind, 2023): generative agent-based modeling grounded by Game Master spatial and social mediation, establishing the precedent for typed social sandboxes.
  • Melting Pot 2.0 (arXiv:2211.13746, agapiou2023meltingpot, Agapiou et al., NeurIPS 2023): multi-agent social dilemma evaluation suite measuring cooperation, free-riding, and resource sustainability across mixed populations.
  • Sequential Social Dilemmas (arXiv:1702.03037, leibo2017ssd, Leibo, Zambaldi, Lanctot, Marecki & Graepel, AAMAS 2017): temporally and spatially extended Markov games with non-linear resource renewal dynamics, moving beyond static normal-form matrix games.
  • The AI Economist (arXiv:2108.02755, zheng2022aieconomist, Zheng, Trott, Srinivasa, Parkes & Socher, Science Advances 2022, 10.1126/sciadv.abk2607): two-level reinforcement learning in dynamic economic sandboxes with taxation, property rights, and public goods.
  • Stratego Multi-Agent Equilibrium (perolat2022stratego, Pérolat et al., Science 2022, 10.1126/science.add4679): deep Nash equilibrium convergence under imperfect information and private state.
  • Diplomacy & Contractual Reasoning (brown2022diplomacy, Meta FAIR Diplomacy Team, Science 2022, 10.1126/science.ade9064): natural language communication coordinated with formal game transition engines and binding contracts.
  • PettingZoo (arXiv:2009.14471, pettingzoo2021, Terry et al., NeurIPS 2021): standard Agent Environment Cycle (AEC) multi-agent interaction API wrapped by SocialSandboxAECEnv.

docs.title: Procedural Stratification & Contrastive Safety Boundaries
docs.text:
• Procgen (arXiv:1912.01588, procgen2020, Cobbe et al., ICML 2020): seed-stratified procedural generation measuring generalisation across held-out seeds rather than environment memorization.
  • OMNI-EPIC (arXiv:2405.15568, omniepic2024, Faldor, Zhang, Cully & Clune, ICLR 2025): contrastive boundary — unlike OMNI-EPIC's unconstrained foundation-model code generation of new game environments, EvolZen explicitly rejects unconstrained engine mutation in favor of bounded, versioned CapabilityPackage records gated by replay, intervention, and containment checks.

docs.title: Legacy Foundations (1984–2010s)
docs.text:
• Sugarscape (epstein1996sugarscape, Epstein & Axtell, Brookings / MIT Press, 1996): foundational agent-based computational economics baseline (resource gathering, metabolic consumption, reproduction, and bilateral trading rules).
  • The Evolution of Cooperation (axelrod1984evolution, Axelrod, Basic Books, 1984): classical iterated game-theoretic cooperation, reciprocity, and norm emergence in multi-agent populations.
  • Causal Intervention & Structural Invariants (pearl2009causality, Pearl, Cambridge University Press, 2009): formal $\text{do}(X=x)$ counterfactual intervention semantics backing evolzen.environment.interventions and counterfactual branch restoration.

The persistent social-sandbox contract, SocialSandboxAECEnv integration, and transfer of these precedents to EvolZen's multi-agent setting are EvolZen design choices and remain untested empirically until Phase 1.1 long-horizon and target-rig experiments are run.

docs.title: Codebase progress match & hardening backlog
docs.text:
• Implemented Phase 1.1 baseline (src/evolzen/environment/, src/evolzen/schemas/world.py, src/evolzen/storage/transition_log.py):
  • SocialSandboxEngine (engine.py) implements Environment and PersistentEnvironment over (state_t, action_t, exogenous_input_t, seed) -> (emission_t, state_{t+1}) with zero hidden mutable state on self, deterministic RNG via derive_rng (world_state.py), deterministic uuid5 transition_id/timestamps, and all 17 ActionType handlers (wait, gather, move, consume, craft, trade, propose_contract, fulfill_contract, found_institution, join_institution, contribute_institution, propose_norm, adopt_norm, assign_role, spawn_offspring, improve_location, register_capability) gated by CapabilityPackage verification flags and world.adulthood_age.
  • Closed frozen schemas (extra="forbid") in schemas/world.py cover all six entity families (LocationNode, WorldAgentState, ArtifactRecord, CapabilityPackage, ContractRecord, InstitutionRecord, NormRecord), ResourceAccounting, WorldState, WorldSnapshot, GrowthEvent, WorldInvariant, InvariantReport, BranchRecord, and InterventionSpec; Transition (schemas/transition.py) includes ExogenousInput and seed.
  • check_invariants (invariants.py), extract_growth_events / summarize_growth (growth.py) across all five GrowthCategory buckets, TransitionLogStore (storage/transition_log.py, SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 DuckDB JSON-only persistence with SHA-256 hash chaining and atomic save_snapshot_and_branch), replay_transitions / replay_from_store / branch_from_snapshot (replay.py), apply_intervention (interventions.py), adapter (observe_features, legal_candidates, action_from_candidate, execute_decision), SocialSandboxAECEnv (pettingzoo_env.py), and run_environment_pilot (pilot.py) are implemented.
  • Landed Stage 1 critical fixes (src/evolzen/environment/{replay,interventions,engine,invariants}.py):
  • replay_transitions passes current_state (not recorded.state) to engine.step so trajectory state divergence cascades and is detected.
  • replay_from_store queries to_tick=up_to_tick and admits transitions with state.tick <= up_to_tick, preserving same_tick=True multi-agent transitions at up_to_tick.
  • apply_intervention supports sequence (list/tuple) indexing in _set_nested_path and reconciles ResourceAccounting.initial_currency on financial state edits.
  • _handle_spawn_offspring and _check_bounded_state count active living agents (sum(1 for a in world.agents.values() if a.alive)) against world.max_agents, eliminating the lineage extinction trap while retaining deceased agent records for immutable lineage auditability.
  • Landed Stage 2 host adapter full 17-action coverage (src/evolzen/environment/adapter.py):
  • adapter.legal_candidates and adapter.action_from_candidate cover all 17 ActionTypes (wait, gather, move, consume, craft, trade, propose_contract, fulfill_contract, found_institution, join_institution, contribute_institution, propose_norm, adopt_norm, assign_role, spawn_offspring, improve_location, register_capability), with dynamic candidate generation and validation in execute_decision.
  • Added cancel_contract:{cid} candidate generation and translation for proposers of open contracts.
  • Landed Stage 3 operational mechanics (src/evolzen/environment/{engine,invariants}.py, src/evolzen/schemas/world.py):
  • Tool Durability & Fatigue Mitigation: Handlers _handle_gather and _handle_improve_location consume tool durability on work actions while halving physical fatigue accumulation.
  • Norm Compliance & Social Friction: _handle_gather checks conservation norms; common-pool depletion below 20% capacity triggers hypocrisy penalties (-0.1 status/social reward) for adopters and community friction (-0.05 status/social reward) for co-located non-adopters, while sustainable harvesting yields compliance bonuses (+0.02).
  • Institutional Trade Fee Withholding & Reserves: _handle_trade withholds institution contribution_rate fees directly into local_inst.currency_reserve while maintaining exact currency conservation; _handle_contribute_institution supports direct currency contributions.
  • Contract Cancellation & Expiration Sweep: Handlers support voluntary cancellation (cancel=True in _handle_fulfill_contract) and automatic expiration sweep (_expire_contracts) for stale open contracts exceeding TTL (100 ticks) or with deceased parties.
  • FR-2 Bounded Collections & Status: Enforced upper bounds on WorldAgentState.status ([0.0, 1.0]) across schemas, invariants, and engine handlers. Enforced capacity bounds (artifacts <= 512, contracts <= 256, institutions <= 64, norms <= 64, capabilities <= 64) in invariants.py and action rejection.
  • Exogenous Provenance: _apply_exogenous records unhandled exogenous event types (unhandled:<kind>) in exogenous_applied transition emissions.
  • Landed Stage 4 PettingZoo AECEnv upgrades & endogenous process attribution (src/evolzen/environment/{pettingzoo_env,engine}.py):
  • PettingZoo Macro-Shocks & Seeding: SocialSandboxAECEnv.step() accepts exogenous_input and deterministic seed kwargs, allowing RL and AEC callers to simulate macroeconomic shocks and seed schedules.
  • TransitionLogStore Hook: SocialSandboxAECEnv.__init__ accepts optional store: TransitionLogStore | None = None and automatically appends every executed transition with DuckDB hash-chain linkage; surfaces env.last_transition and env.store.
  • Expanded 16-Action Discrete Space: Expanded _act_space to Discrete(16) with full typed translation and action masks for trade, institution joining, contributions, norm proposals, norm adoptions, and reproduction alongside physical foraging/crafting.
  • Endogenous Process Growth Attribution: Added _expand_endogenous_ecology in engine.py, passively expanding carrying capacity by 1 for undisturbed flourishing ecosystems (shock_factor == 1.0, full resource capacity, next_tick % 50 == 0), activating the previously dormant GrowthAttribution.ENDOGENOUS_PROCESS emitter in growth.py.
  • Open Phase 1.1 production-hardening backlog (empirical success metrics remain unmeasured):
  • Untested verification & pilot gates: All 18 failure branches in invariants.py, Hypothesis property-based tests for engine/invariants/replay, and long-horizon multi-generation and target-rig hardware pilots remain untested; Phase 1.1 empirical success metrics are not met.

docs.title: Phase 1.2 — The Agents
docs.text:
Subsystem: evolzen.agents Code: src/evolzen/agents/

Detailed design: developmental agents. Implemented increment: agents/development/ and schemas/development.py contain a numerical lifecycle/learning/teaching/archive baseline. LLM training and full population/world integration remain pending.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Populate the persistent world with 10–30 active cognitive agents plus optional deterministic background population processes. Each active agent has an explicit behavioral/social profile: needs, drives, skills, roles, affiliations, memory scope, communication channels, norms, capabilities, and lineage. “All types of people” is operationalized as coverage of this ontology, not as a claim to reproduce real human demographics or psychology.

Drive vectors are evolved on the vector itself, never by literal crossover of independently trained neural weights. Quality-Diversity selection preserves declared behavioral and social descriptors. Self-modification is optional in the first baseline and, when enabled, is sandboxed and accepted only after held-out improvement plus invariant checks.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• exactly eight birth-randomized motivational coordinates: pride, greed, lust, envy, gluttony, wrath, sloth, Null; a safe bounded equation family rather than generated source programs;
  • child/adolescent/adult/elder/dead stages on a world clock, with competence measured separately;
  • personal outcome learning and living-parent advice, without copying mastery at birth;

  • bounded numeric temperament inheritance and validation-gated behavioral archive admission;

  • an AgentProfile schema and an explicit descriptor map;

  • population and lineage snapshots;
  • QD archive coverage, occupancy, persistence, extinction, replacement, specialization, and communication metrics;
  • a sparse communication/trade graph and non-authoritative role structure; and
  • a hardware pilot that records model memory, token throughput, action latency, and scheduling overhead on the actual rig.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text:
First satisfy developmental primitive gates: reproducible equations, action/feedback adaptation, life boundaries, parent teaching, and archive safety. Then measure cultural transfer, age-versus-experience and eight-axis controls on held-out worlds/families. Passing unit tests does not satisfy the population success metric below.

A 10–30-agent population runs stably for at least five generations, maintains measurable coverage across the declared descriptor map, and produces at least two persistent role/specialization patterns without collapsing to one strategy. Any self-modification improvement is reported separately from population diversity.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
• Peer-reviewed IEEE / journal foundations: Oudeyer, Kaplan & Hafner (2007, IEEE TEVC, DOI:10.1109/TEVC.2006.890271) for intrinsic motivation in developmental learning; Merrick (2010, IEEE TAMD/TCDS, DOI:10.1109/TAMD.2010.2051435) for comparative intrinsic value-system benchmarking; Santucci, Baldassarre & Mirolli (2016, IEEE TCDS, DOI:10.1109/TCDS.2016.2538961) for goal-discovering developmental architectures; Vassiliades, Chatzilygeroudis & Mouret (2018, IEEE TEVC, DOI:10.1109/TEVC.2017.2735550) for CVT-MAP-Elites scaling to higher-dimensional behavioral descriptors; Pugh, Soros & Stanley (2016, Frontiers in Robotics and AI, DOI:10.3389/frobt.2016.00040) for separating quality from behavioral diversity; Hayes et al. (2022, JAAMAS, DOI:10.1007/s10458-022-09552-y) for MORL linear vs. non-linear Chebyshev scalarization; Keramati & Gutkin (2014, eLife, DOI:10.7554/eLife.04811) for homeostatic drive-reduction utility; Colas et al. (2022, JAIR, arXiv:2012.09830) for autotelic goal-conditioned agents; Asadi & Littman (2017, ICML, arXiv:1612.05628) for Mellowmax softmax stability.
  • Conference / preprints: Darwin Gödel Machine (arXiv:2505.22954, ICLR 2026), Hyperagents (arXiv:2603.19461, preprint), Quality-Diversity with Limited Resources (Wang et al., ICML 2024, arXiv:2406.03731), Cook et al. (Artificial Generational Intelligence, arXiv:2406.00392, 2024), and Generative Agents (Park et al., ACM UIST 2023 / arXiv:2304.03442). Continual experience replay (Rolnick et al., CLEAR, NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:1811.11682) governs Phase 2.1 rehearsal replay, while Phase 1.2 runtime employs verified contextual EMA outcome estimation and intergenerational manual teaching (teach_manual).

The eight-drive ontology, descriptor map, and transfer from these precedents to a persistent social sandbox remain untested; cited diversity-collapse studies are treated as hypotheses.

docs.title: Research context & breakthroughs
docs.text:
• Intrinsic motivation & developmental stages: IEEE TEVC (Oudeyer et al., 2007) and IEEE TCDS (Santucci et al., 2016) formalize competence-progress and autonomous goal discovery across developmental lifetimes—highlighting that EvolZen's current greedy candidate ranking (decide) is a numerical baseline requiring a controlled exploration comparison.
  • Quality-Diversity scaling: MAP-Elites and CVT-MAP-Elites (IEEE TEVC, 2018; Pugh et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2024) replace single-objective fitness selection with behavioral repertoire maintenance, directly countering LLM multi-agent homogenization (ACL 2026 Findings diversitycollapse2026).
  • Self-modification & metacognitive risk: DGM (ICLR 2026) and Hyperagents (arXiv:2603.19461) show empirical archive-gated self-editing and emergent persistent memory structures, underscoring why self-modification in EvolZen is gated by DevelopmentArchive and evolzen.containment.Sandbox.

docs.title: Codebase progress match
docs.text:
• Implemented unified developmental agent architecture (src/evolzen/agents/, src/evolzen/schemas/):
  • Identity & profile: AgentProfile (schemas/agent_profile.py), replacing the legacy five-axis DriveVector with rich social, institutional, norm, and behavioral descriptor tracking.
  • Developmental runtime: Agent (agents/agent.py), unifying AgentProfile, AgentDevelopmentState, lifecycle staging (stage_at), and host-adapter integration.
  • Decision policy & exploration: Augmented Chebyshev scalarization (brain.py), UCB1 epistemic exploration bonus, and Mellowmax temperature sampling.
  • Structured LLM inference: InferenceBackend & TransformersBackend (agents/inference.py), providing outlines-constrained schema-valid action generation with deterministic safe fallback.
  • Scaled quality-diversity archive: CVTArchive & QualityDiversityArchive (agents/qd_archive.py), implementing Centroidal Voronoi Tessellations across $k$-D behavioral descriptors (vassiliades2018cvtmape).
  • Sandboxed self-modification: SelfModificationProposal & evaluate_proposal (agents/self_modification.py), enforcing default-deny execution inside evolzen.containment.Sandbox.
  • Population scheduler & teaching: PopulationScheduler (agents/scheduler.py), orchestrating generational rollouts, living-parent skill advice, recipe manual transmission (teach_manual), and DuckDB transition persistence.
  • Comprehensive test coverage: Covered by 58 passing test cases across tests/agents/ (including test_agent.py, test_inference.py, test_manual_teaching.py, test_qd_archive.py, test_self_modification.py, test_population_integration.py, and tests/agents/development/).
  • Implemented Phase 1.1 environment host bridge (src/evolzen/environment/adapter.py, engine.py, pettingzoo_env.py): SocialSandboxEngine, WorldState/ActionType (schemas/world.py), SocialSandboxAECEnv, and adapter (observe_features, legal_candidates, action_from_candidate, execute_decision).
  • Retired legacy path: Legacy 5-axis DriveVector (schemas/drive_vector.py, agents/drive_vector.py) cleanly retired per Option A architectural consensus.
  • Open alignment & empirical items:
  • Multi-generation empirical benchmarking runs on hardware pilot;
  • GPU tensor-parallel live serving via VLLMBackend;
  • Expanding adapter.legal_candidates from 7 to all 17 actions in SocialSandboxEngine.

docs.title: Phase 1.3 — Economy & Knowledge Layer
docs.text: Subsystem: evolzen.economy Code: src/evolzen/economy/

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Add resource flows, contracts, markets, institutions, norms, and knowledge transfer to the persistent world. The layer must make specialization and cooperation possible without making shared manuals an unexamined, recursively self-training channel.

The “real-data floor” is a provenance requirement, not a claim that a synthetic world has real human data. Sources are labeled as human-authored/external material, human demonstrations, independently generated simulator traces, or model-generated material. The floor and its sampling budget are configuration and report fields.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• a domain-scoped currency/resource ledger and market mechanism;
  • contracts, institutions, and norm proposals with explicit adoption/rejection events;
  • falsifiable, revisable manuals with evidence, provenance, scope, and revision history;
  • forward/backward knowledge-transfer measurements; and
  • world-health checks for resource conservation, concentration, collapse, and recovery from shocks.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text: At least one durable institution or norm and two distinct specialization patterns emerge across five generations; manuals are revised after induced falsifications; and the configured provenance floor remains satisfied without a collapse in population or world diversity.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
• Peer-reviewed journals: Shumailov et al. (2024, Nature, DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-07566-y) demonstrating recursive model collapse on synthetic generations; Zheng et al. (The AI Economist, Science Advances 2022, DOI:10.1126/sciadv.abk2607) demonstrating two-level multi-agent economic equilibrium and emergent specialization.
  • Preprints / vendor reports: Economy of Minds (arXiv:2606.02859, preprint) and vendor manual-transfer reports (agno2026manual).

Vendor-reported manual-transfer results are treated as narrow exposure-regime case studies; replication and economic emergence in EvolZen are untested.

docs.title: Research context & breakthroughs
docs.text:
• Model collapse & provenance floors: Shumailov et al. (Nature, 2024) proved that recursively training models on prior synthetic outputs erodes distribution tails and diversity—directly motivating ManualStore's hard provenance separation and EconomySettings.real_data_floor.
  • Emergent economic mechanisms: The AI Economist (Science Advances, 2022) demonstrated that coupled agent learning and economic policy design yield interpretable specialization and inequality/health trade-offs, motivating evolzen.economy's resource-concentration and shock-recovery metrics.

docs.title: Codebase progress match
docs.text:
• Schemas (src/evolzen/schemas/manual.py, world.py): ManualEntryStatus, ManualEntry, Manual, ProvenanceSource, and ProvenanceRecord are fully implemented, tracking source origin, SHA-256 digests, revision lineages, and evidence links.
  • Implemented Phase 1.3 Economy baseline (src/evolzen/economy/):
  • Market & Order Book (market.py): Integer currency balances (NonNegInt) aligned with WorldAgentState.currency and InstitutionRecord.currency_reserve; Hayekian dynamic scarcity pricing (quote_price, citing Qi et al. 2026); continuous double auction OrderBook matching bids/asks at crossing midpoints with institutional fee withholding; typed ActionType.TRADE action construction (create_trade_action); and direct state settlement (settle_in_world) maintaining exact conservation.
  • Manuals & Provenance Floor (manuals.py): Falsifiable natural-language manuals with empirical falsification (falsify), revision (revise), and confirmation (confirm) chains; automated non-model provenance fraction computation (calculate_real_fraction) and generation corpus gating (verify_generation_corpus, citing Shumailov et al. 2024); forward knowledge transfer gain measurement (measure_knowledge_transfer); and backward compatibility degradation testing (verify_backward_compatibility).
  • Economic Health & Specialization Metrics (metrics.py): Gini coefficient of wealth inequality (compute_gini_coefficient, citing Zheng et al. 2022); Herfindahl-Hirschman Index and Shannon entropy for division of labor (compute_specialization_index); shock recovery and resilience ratio computation (compute_shock_recovery); and macroscopic health evaluation (evaluate_economic_health).
  • Test coverage (tests/economy/): 63 passing tests across test_provenance.py, test_manuals.py, test_market.py, and test_metrics.py (100% statement coverage of evolzen.economy).
  • Downstream integration & empirical gates:
  • Direct integration into developmental teaching passes (evolzen.agents.development.teach_manual, Agent.teach_manual, and Lesson.manual_entry) implemented and verified with 10 unit tests in tests/agents/test_manual_teaching.py.
  • Multi-generation empirical runs across five generations measuring emergent specialization and durable institutions on DGX/AGX hardware remain untested; success metric remains unmeasured.

docs.title: Phase 1.4 — Directed Exploration & Verified Hypothesis Formation
docs.text: Subsystem: evolzen.exploration Code: src/evolzen/exploration/

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Use an actor/synthesizer/verifier loop to propose typed rules and capability packages for the persistent world. Exploration is prioritized by a measured explanation gap over agent types, mechanics, and world-growth categories. An off-the-shelf coding-agent harness may serve as the synthesizer, but generated code is untrusted and must execute only inside evolzen.containment.Sandbox.

Exact replay is necessary but not sufficient. Promotion requires replay on held-out transition combinations, at least one controlled intervention, declared resource bounds, and an explicit validity context.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• actor probes and ontology/explanation-gap prioritization;
  • typed hypothesis and capability-package schemas;
  • sandboxed synthesis and execution;
  • replay, held-out-combination, intervention, and resource-bound verification; and
  • false-promotion, false-rejection, and exploration-cost measurements.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text: Verified hypotheses beat a no-exploration-strategy baseline on held-out transitions and controlled interventions, while false promotions remain below a pre-registered threshold and no hypothesis can mutate the engine outside the versioned capability boundary.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
• Peer-reviewed journals / conferences: Romera-Paredes et al. (FunSearch, Nature 2024, DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06924-6) for evaluator-gated LLM evolutionary program search; Pathak et al. (ICML 2017, arXiv:1705.05363) for self-supervised prediction-error curiosity; Wang et al. (Voyager, TMLR 2023) for self-verifying code synthesis.
  • Preprints: OPINE-World (arXiv:2607.01531), Tycho (arXiv:2607.28287), and Executable World Models for ARC-AGI-3 (arXiv:2605.05138).

Benchmark results in isolated games or math problems do not establish transfer to a persistent social sandbox; that transfer is an explicit EvolZen experiment and is untested.

docs.title: Research context & breakthroughs
docs.text:
• Verifier-gated program search: FunSearch (Nature, 2024) and Executable World Models (arXiv:2605.05138) showed that pairing LLM code generators with deterministic evaluators discovers novel verifiable programs while avoiding ungrounded hallucinations.
  • Ontology-error & curiosity prioritization: Pathak et al. (ICML 2017) introduced forward-model prediction error as an intrinsic exploration signal, while OPINE-World (arXiv:2607.01531) and Tycho (arXiv:2607.28287) prioritize probing actions that falsify current programmatic world hypotheses.

docs.title: Codebase progress match
docs.text:
• Upstream Phase 1.1 contracts implemented: SocialSandboxEngine, replay_transitions, apply_intervention, TransitionLogStore, and CapabilityPackage (with evidence_id, verified_replay, verified_intervention, verified_containment) are implemented in evolzen.environment, evolzen.schemas.world, and evolzen.storage.
  • Actor (src/evolzen/exploration/actor.py): Selects probes by ontology/explanation gap (1 test in tests/exploration/test_actor.py).
  • Synthesizer (src/evolzen/exploration/synthesizer.py): CandidateRule, Synthesizer protocol, and TemplateRuleSynthesizer generating executable Python prediction functions from observed transitions (4 tests in tests/exploration/test_synthesizer.py).
  • Verifier (src/evolzen/exploration/verifier.py): Implemented Verifier with VerificationReport executing rule hypotheses exclusively inside evolzen.containment.Sandbox. Supports exact-match replay across held-out transitions, counterfactual intervention verification (verify_intervention), and capability promotion (promote_to_capability_package) accepted by CapabilityGovernor and SocialSandboxEngine (9 tests in tests/exploration/test_verifier.py).
  • Total test coverage: 14 tests passing across tests/exploration/.
  • Open cross-phase alignment items:
  • Multi-generational autonomous coding-agent LLM harness benchmarks on hardware rig. Empirical exploration transfer remains untested.

docs.title: Phase 1.5 — Growing Rule Library
docs.text: Subsystem: evolzen.library Code: src/evolzen/library/

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Store verified rules and capability packages as immutable historical entries without erasing rules that were valid in earlier world contexts. New versions may supersede old entries explicitly when a world mechanic changes; routing must respect validity context and never silently rewrite history.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• immutable rule/capability records with provenance and evidence links;
  • validity intervals or context predicates;
  • explicit supersession and deprecation links;
  • capability package persistence and bidirectional world synchronization;
  • a held-out transition/intervention regression bank supporting direct transition log ingestion;
  • schema version guards preventing forward-incompatible corruption; and
  • audit records for spawn, route, promotion, supersession, and rejection decisions.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text: Historical entries remain readable and replayable across at least three rounds of additions; new entries improve held-out performance; and any supersession is explicit, reversible, and attributable to a measured change in world context.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
• Peer-reviewed journals: Ferguson (1973, Annals of Statistics) motivating the spawn-when-inadequate routing analogy; Wang et al. (2024, IEEE TPAMI, DOI:10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3367329) surveying continual-learning isolation and memory architectures; Wang et al. (Voyager, TMLR 2023) demonstrating compositional skill libraries to mitigate forgetting.

The implemented library is not claimed to be a Bayesian Dirichlet-process model; its routing, supersession, and reversal policies are EvolZen design choices.

docs.title: Research context & breakthroughs
docs.text: • External skill libraries vs. parameter drift: IEEE TPAMI (Wang et al., 2024) categorizes parameter-isolation and external-memory architectures as the primary defense against catastrophic forgetting, while Voyager (TMLR, 2023) demonstrates non-overwriting skill libraries for lifelong embodied agents. EvolZen extends that model with explicit ValidityContext, provenance separation, and reversible supersession links (env-v1 → env-v2) required when environment rules legitimately evolve.

docs.title: Codebase progress match
docs.text:
• Implemented subsystem (src/evolzen/schemas/library.py, src/evolzen/library/, src/evolzen/config.py, configs/library.yaml): Full append-only DuckDB persistence (LibraryStore), JSONL file-locked AuditLog (SPAWN, ROUTE, PROMOTE, SUPERSEDE, REVERT, DEPRECATE, REJECT, REGRESSION_CHECK), context compatibility predicates (validity.py), RuleLibrary orchestrator, and fixture-based RegressionBank.
  • Capability package persistence & world synchronization: Native persistence of Phase 1.1 CapabilityPackage records in LibraryStore.capability_packages, status lifecycle management, and bidirectional world synchronization (export_capabilities_to_world, import_capabilities_from_world).
  • Transition log regression ingestion: Direct ingestion of recorded environment transitions into RegressionBank from Transition objects and DuckDB TransitionLogStore, linking empirical environment evidence directly to regression fixtures without uncontained code execution.
  • Schema version verification: Explicit schema_meta table tracking and SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 guards rejecting forward-incompatible database schemas.
  • Verified tests (tests/library/): Full test suite across schemas, persistence, audit, validity, regression fixtures, orchestrator, and capability integration (test_capability_integration.py).
  • Scope / untested boundary: Default routing uses difflib.SequenceMatcher guarded by is_applicable until Phase 2.3 provides learned embeddings; RegressionBank.check_rule validates pre-verified serialisable fixtures without executing RuleEntry.code. Live replay against evolzen.exploration.verifier (Phase 1.4), evolzen.containment.Sandbox (Phase 2.2), and dynamic code generation remains untested until Phases 1.4 and 2.2 are operational.
