docs.title: Phase 2.1 — Grounded Predictor
docs.text: Subsystem: evolzen.predictor Code: src/evolzen/predictor/

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Build a grounded predictor of world transitions, agent actions, and declared latent profile variables. Start with a supervised/action-prediction baseline; add PPO/GRPO-style planning only after its incremental value is measurable. Train against replayable outcomes, not another model's approval, and protect updates with a declared rehearsal budget.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• next-state, outcome, and action prediction baselines;
  • optional policy-gradient planning with explicit reward decomposition;
  • replay/rehearsal and checkpoint rollback;
  • forward transfer, backward transfer, forgetting, adaptation latency, and update-cost metrics; and
  • separate tests for prediction, intervention response, and planning efficiency.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text: The predictor reports held-out transition and intervention performance plus longitudinal transfer and forgetting curves. No fixed accuracy target is accepted in advance; the baseline and all update costs are reported.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
• Peer-reviewed journals / conferences: Wang et al. (2024, IEEE TPAMI, DOI:10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3367329) for continual-learning theory and replay/regularization taxonomy; Rolnick et al. (CLEAR, NeurIPS 2019, arXiv:1811.11682) for experience replay in continual RL; Kirkpatrick et al. (EWC, PNAS 2017, DOI:10.1073/pnas.1611835114) for parameter-regularization baselines.
  • Preprints: DeepSeekMath / GRPO (Shao et al., arXiv:2402.03300), CLaaS (arXiv:2606.05559), and TFGN (arXiv:2605.15053).

Their reported metrics are not imported as universal baselines; matched EvolZen measurements are required and remain untested.

docs.title: Research context & breakthroughs
docs.text:
• Replay & continual RL: CLEAR (NeurIPS, 2019) showed that mixing on-policy updates with bounded off-policy behavioral-cloning replay prevents catastrophic forgetting in sequential environments—directly grounding RehearsalBuffer. IEEE TPAMI (Wang et al., 2024) formalizes measuring forward transfer, backward transfer, and spurious forgetting together.
  • Critic-free policy optimization (GRPO): DeepSeekMath (arXiv:2402.03300) replaced heavy value networks with group-relative normalized outcome rewards—providing a lower-memory candidate RL optimizer for Planner once supervised world-transition baselines exist.

docs.title: Codebase progress match
docs.text:
• Upstream Phase 1.1 data & intervention sources: TransitionLogStore (evolzen.storage.transition_log) and apply_intervention (evolzen.environment.interventions) are implemented to supply recorded Transition streams and counterfactual world edits.
  • Supervised dynamics baseline (src/evolzen/predictor/dynamics.py): WorldDynamicsPredictor implements supervised prediction of (predicted_emission, predicted_next_state) with 8-dimensional reward decomposition, acceptance classification, and agent numeric state delta tracking (5 tests in tests/predictor/test_dynamics.py).
  • Rehearsal buffer & continual metrics (src/evolzen/predictor/rehearsal_buffer.py): RehearsalBuffer implements CLEAR-style mixed on-policy / off-policy batch sampling (sample_clear_batch) and DuckDB streaming from TransitionLogStore. ContinualMetricsTracker computes formal Backward Transfer (BWT), Forward Transfer (FWT), and catastrophic forgetting matrices (6 tests in tests/predictor/test_rehearsal_buffer.py).
  • Planner (src/evolzen/predictor/planner.py): Planner implements critic-free GRPO policy optimization (DeepSeekMath, arXiv:2402.03300) with group-relative advantage normalization, KL damping, and plan_action optimization against verifiable environment outcomes (5 tests in tests/predictor/test_planner.py).
  • Overall status: Phase 2.1 implementation complete with 16 tests passing in tests/predictor/. Empirical curves remain untested until execution on target hardware.

  • predictor subsystem docs for the code-level map and build order.

docs.title: Phase 2.2 — Verification Gate & Containment
docs.text: Subsystem: evolzen.containment Code: src/evolzen/containment/

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Provide the execution boundary for all agent-generated and synthesized code, and the promotion boundary for new capability packages. Exact replay/intervention checks are reused from Phase 1.4. The security design is fail-closed: static default-deny policy is authoritative, while behavior-sensitive governance may tighten access but may not bypass the static policy.

The Sandbox protocol can be developed early, but a real containment claim requires a deployed Firecracker/gVisor-backed executor and target-host acceptance tests. The interface alone is not a security result.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• capability-scoped default-deny policy;
  • hardware-isolated backend integration;
  • resource, filesystem, network, subprocess, syscall, and credential controls;
  • tamper-evident action and governance logging;
  • evaluator separation and deterministic recovery; and
  • deliberate violation tests for kill-switch latency, cleanup, rollback, and restart.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text: Interface, backend, and target-host threat-model tests each pass: no unlogged action, no unbounded resource use, fail-closed denial, bounded kill-switch latency, clean recovery, and preserved audit logs. The report states which layer was actually tested.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
• Peer-reviewed systems conference: Agache et al. (Firecracker, USENIX NSDI 2020) for KVM-backed microVM isolation (~5 MB memory overhead, millisecond startup, minimal virtio device model).
  • Preprints: CORAL (arXiv:2604.01658), Sidik & Rokach (arXiv:2604.11839), and Safety Must Precede the Deployment of Open-Ended AI (arXiv:2502.04512).

The security of a specific backend on the stated hardware is untested until deployment validation.

docs.title: Research context & breakthroughs
docs.text:
• MicroVM vs. shared-kernel containers: Firecracker (USENIX NSDI, 2020) established that dedicated KVM virtualization with a Rust VMM and stripped legacy hardware avoids the shared-kernel attack surface of containers while preserving lightweight startup—justifying why SECURITY.md forbids treating plain subprocesses or shared-kernel containers as a final containment boundary for evolzen.agents / evolzen.exploration code execution.
  • Fail-closed learned governance: Recent agent-governance proposals (arXiv:2604.11839) motivate dynamic risk tightening strictly inside static default-deny capability bounds (CapabilityGovernor).

docs.title: Codebase progress match
docs.text:
• Governance (src/evolzen/containment/governance.py): Implemented CapabilityGovernor supporting dynamic tightening via record_violation() (immediate capability revocation and violation logging), capability verification gating (verify_capability_package() enforcing fail-closed verified_containment and boundary invariants), audit trail export (export_audit_trail()), and cryptographic tamper-evident SHA-256 hash chaining (audit_hash()). Fully tested across 8 unit tests in tests/containment/test_governance.py.
  • Sandbox (src/evolzen/containment/sandbox.py): Implemented runtime-checkable Sandbox protocol and GVisorSandbox driver using runsc with --net=none, memory limit ceiling, wall-time timeouts, structured JSON (Emission, State) return channels (ExecutionResult.get_json_output()), and fail-closed denial (strictly raising RuntimeError when runsc is unavailable without bare subprocess fallback). Implemented is_gvisor_available() host probe.
  • Test Harness & Mocking (tests/containment/conftest.py & tests/containment/test_sandbox.py): Implemented MockSandbox test fixture providing hermetic sandbox simulation with invocation history tracking, timeout/OOM simulation, and deterministic structured output extraction. Verified across 21 unit tests covering frozen ExecutionResult, JSON decoding, security flags, fail-closed absence handling, and mocked/live execution.
  • Configuration (src/evolzen/config.py & configs/containment.yaml): Implemented ContainmentSettings with backend, runsc_path, default_timeout_seconds, default_resource_ceiling_mb, and enforce_containment.
  • Open cross-phase alignment items:
  • Wire CapabilityGovernor to SocialSandboxEngine._handle_register_capability and WorldAgentState, linking GovernanceEvent records with TransitionLogStore.
  • Wire Verifier (Phase 1.4) and SocialSandboxEngine (Phase 1.1) to execute untrusted code through Sandbox / GVisorSandbox (or MockSandbox in CI). Live target-host security remains untested until hardware deployment validation on Linux hosts with runsc installed.

docs.title: Phase 2.3 — Recognition Model & Growing Library
docs.text: Subsystem: evolzen.recognition Code: src/evolzen/recognition/

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Test a proposed JEPA-style state representation plus DreamCoder-style wake-sleep operator learning against simpler baselines in the persistent social sandbox. The combination is a research hypothesis, not a validated architecture and not evidence of general intelligence.

The rule library is routed sparsely for efficiency, while the manual layer remains a provenance- tracked fast memory tier. Neither routing confidence nor manual fluency is a verification result.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• a state-representation baseline before JEPA;
  • JEPA-only, wake-sleep-only, combined, and no-recognition conditions;
  • manual-on/manual-off conditions with matched exposure;
  • sparse routing with auditable expert selection; and
  • persistent-world and fresh-world evaluation cells with confidence intervals and compute/data budgets.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text: The recognition condition improves adaptation latency or success on at least one pre-registered track without unacceptable regression on the other. All ablation cells, including null or negative results, are reported.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
• Peer-reviewed conferences & IEEE journals: Assran et al. (I-JEPA, CVPR 2023, arXiv:2301.08243) for latent joint-embedding predictive learning without pixel reconstruction; Ellis et al. (DreamCoder, PLDI 2021; Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 2023) for wake-sleep program-library compression; Johnson, Douze & Jégou (2019, IEEE Transactions on Big Data, DOI:10.1109/TBDATA.2019.2921572) for FAISS similarity search backing EmbeddingRouter.
  • Preprints: LeJEPA (arXiv:2511.08544), When Does LeJEPA Learn a World Model? (arXiv:2605.26379), and Do Neurons Dream of Primitive Operators? (arXiv:2603.25975).

The proposed combination and its transfer to a persistent social sandbox are untested; cited preprints are hypothesis sources, not validation of EvolZen.

docs.title: Research context & breakthroughs
docs.text:
• Latent predictive encoders (I-JEPA / LeJEPA): CVPR 2023 (arXiv:2301.08243) showed predicting masked latent representations avoids brittle pixel/token reconstruction, while arXiv:2511.08544 simplifies regularization—motivating JEPAEncoder strictly as an ablated hypothesis against symbolic/MLP baselines.
  • Wake-sleep operator abstraction + IEEE FAISS routing: DreamCoder (PLDI 2021) alternates task solving (wake) with library refactoring and dreamed replays (sleep), paired here with IEEE Transactions on Big Data (Johnson et al., 2019) inner-product indexing (faiss-cpu / faiss-gpu-cu12) to retrieve candidate RuleEntry experts from evolzen.library.RuleLibrary.

docs.title: Codebase progress match
docs.text:
• Upstream contracts available: Phase 1.1 WorldState, TransitionLogStore, and adapter.observe_features, plus Phase 1.5 RuleLibrary (evolzen.library), are implemented.
  • Routing (src/evolzen/recognition/embedding_router.py, moe_library.py): EmbeddingRouter implements sentence-transformers + faiss.IndexFlatIP indexing (1 optional-dep test in tests/recognition/test_embedding_router.py); SparseMoELibrary wires ExpertRouter to evolzen.library.RuleLibrary.get returning list[RuleEntry] (2 tests in tests/recognition/test_moe_library.py).
  • Grounded JEPA encoder (src/evolzen/recognition/jepa.py): GroundedJEPAEncoder implements LeJEPA/I-JEPA self-supervised continuous state representation learning with invariance and variance-regularization objectives (4 tests in tests/recognition/test_jepa.py).
  • Wake-sleep program abstraction (src/evolzen/recognition/wake_sleep.py): WakeSleepLearner implements wake hypothesis proposal (reusing verified rules or synthesizing candidates) and sleep MDL compression refactoring fused with JEPA (3 tests in tests/recognition/test_wake_sleep.py).
  • Ablation matrix harness (src/evolzen/recognition/ablations.py): AblationRunner implements the 4-cell matrix (Baseline, JEPA-only, Wake-Sleep-only, Combined) with 95% confidence intervals and Markdown reporting (5 tests in tests/recognition/test_ablations.py).
  • Overall status: Phase 2.3 implementation complete with 15 tests passing in tests/recognition/. Empirical transfer curves remain untested until execution on target hardware.

docs.title: Phase 2.4-2.5 — Held-Out Generalization Testing & Evaluation/Publication
docs.text: Subsystem: evolzen.evaluation Code: src/evolzen/evaluation/

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Evaluate two distinct outcomes:

  1. Persistent-world growth: whether the world produces durable artifacts, capabilities, institutions, norms, markets, roles, and lineages while preserving replayability and world health over long runs.
  2. Fresh-world adaptation: whether the learning system adapts efficiently to held-out world seeds and held-out mechanic combinations with no accumulated history.

Use EvolZen Action Efficiency (EAE) for the second track. EAE is inspired by the rationale of RHAE but must not be called an ARC-AGI-3 score unless the official task and scoring protocol are followed exactly. Any human/frontier reference must receive the same observations, actions, and time budget.

docs.title: What you build
docs.text:
• persistent-world runs with seed-stratified longitudinal reports;
  • fresh-world generation with held-out seeds and mechanic combinations;
  • reused-versus-fresh exposure controls;
  • EAE scoring, adaptation latency, cost, and failure accounting;
  • diversity, growth, health, extinction, and recovery reports; and
  • a structured report in which every number traces to a pre-registered metric.

docs.title: Success metric
docs.text: Both tracks produce reproducible results across seeds, all ablations are reported, and the final report separates world growth from fresh adaptation rather than collapsing them into one headline.

docs.title: Citations
docs.text:
• Peer-reviewed conference: Cobbe et al. (Procgen, ICML 2020, DOI:10.48550/arXiv.1912.01588) demonstrating why procedurally generated held-out seeds and level distributions are necessary to measure genuine generalization rather than memorization.
  • Preprints & benchmark specs: Chollet (On the Measure of Intelligence, arXiv:1911.01547), Chollet et al. (ARC-AGI-2, arXiv:2505.11831), ARC Prize Foundation ARC-AGI-3 (arcprize2026), and Agno vendor report (agno2026manual, exposure-regime case study).

The EAE protocol and two-track persistent-vs-fresh evaluation remain untested until measured.

docs.title: Research context & breakthroughs
docs.text: • Procedural OOD splits & public-vs-fresh gap: Procgen (ICML 2020) showed agents trained on fixed levels fail sharply on procedurally generated held-out distributions, while Chollet's On the Measure of Intelligence and ARC-AGI-2 (arXiv:2505.11831) formalize measuring skill-acquisition efficiency on novel rule compositions rather than memorized benchmarks. This directly anchors EvolZen's mandatory reused-vs-fresh reporting split.

docs.title: Codebase progress match
docs.text:
• Upstream Phase 1.1 world & growth metrics: SocialSandboxEngine (PersistentEnvironment, reset(seed=..., run_id=...), snapshot, restore), GrowthEvent / summarize_growth, and InvariantReport are implemented in evolzen.environment and evolzen.schemas.world.
  • Procedural environment generator (src/evolzen/evaluation/procedural_env_gen.py): ProceduralEnvironmentGenerator generates seed-stratified, non-reused environment instances with varying topologies, carrying capacities, and agent counts (4 tests in tests/evaluation/test_procedural_env_gen.py).
  • Dual-track evaluation engine (src/evolzen/evaluation/dual_track.py): DualTrackRunner separates persistent-world growth (survival, invariants, Gini inequality, and growth events) from fresh-world EAE action efficiency and reports the mandatory reused-vs-fresh exposure gap (3 tests in tests/evaluation/test_dual_track.py).
  • Report & scorer (src/evolzen/evaluation/report.py, rhae_scorer.py): EvaluationReport container and RHAEScorer aggregating relative action efficiency against human baselines (6 tests in tests/evaluation/test_report.py and test_rhae_scorer.py).
  • Unified Typer CLI (src/evolzen/cli/main.py): Dispatches evolzen run, evolzen train, evolzen evaluate, evolzen replay, and evolzen inspect (7 tests in tests/cli/test_cli.py).
  • Overall status: Phases 2.4/2.5 complete with 20 tests passing across tests/evaluation/ and tests/cli/. Empirical evaluation curves remain untested until execution on target hardware.

docs.title: docs/research/
docs.text:
The literature this project's design is accountable to.

File Contents literature-review.md The six research threads the design draws on, and which subsystem each one shapes. landscape.md Comparative landscape and source-status notes; benchmark numbers are dated and should not be treated as permanent baselines. design-evolution.md Historical record of design changes from the original voxel/observer blueprint. design-audit.md Section-by-section audit of the supplied blueprints against the repository and the revised persistent-world goal. docs-and-codebase-audit.md Full docs/ structural validation, verified IEEE/ML citations per phase, and codebase progress match. objectives-and-evaluation.md Research questions, hypotheses, baselines, evaluation tracks, split rules, and decision gates. references.bib Full BibTeX citation list.

For the original developmental-brain design, use the agent evidence ledger and matched evaluation protocol. The inspected primary sources support component precedents, not the psychological validity of the seven-sins-plus-Null basis.

Standing rule: a design choice in this codebase either traces to an entry in references.bib, or is explicitly flagged as untested. Each source is labeled as peer-reviewed, preprint, vendor report, or unverified. If you add a citation-backed mechanism, add the citation here first.

docs.title: Design Audit — Supplied Blueprints vs. Repository and Revised Goal
docs.text:
Audit date: 2026-10-21 Scope: the supplied master overview, segmented plan, PRDs, voxel-engine appendix, and technical summary, compared with the repository's docs/, AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md, and the revised goal: an independently growing game world populated by diverse synthetic agents.

No code or tests are required for this audit. The repository remains a Phase 0 scaffold.

Status update (2026-11-12, branch env @ 81ee6eb): Phase 0 scaffolding is no longer the current repository state. Three code baselines are now implemented and unit-tested: (1) Phase 1.1 (evolzen.environment + evolzen.schemas.world + evolzen.storage.transition_log) — SocialSandboxEngine, 17 ActionType handlers, invariants, growth ledger, DuckDB TransitionLogStore, replay, interventions, adapter, SocialSandboxAECEnv, and run_environment_pilot; (2) Phase 1.2 numerical core (evolzen.agents.development + evolzen.schemas.development) — deterministic 8-drive BirthGenome/Motive/LifeStage/decide/observe/teach/DevelopmentArchive; and (3) Phase 1.5 (evolzen.library) — immutable versioned rule library, ValidityContext, supersession, JSONL audit trail, and fixture RegressionBank. Downstream subsystems (agents LLM/QD/scheduler, economy, exploration, predictor, containment, recognition, evaluation, cli) remain stubs or isolated prototypes, Phase 1.1 hardening items (ENV-01–ENV-08, partial mechanics, 7/17 legal_candidates coverage) remain open, and no empirical gate (G1–G6) or target-rig pilot result is claimed yet. The 2026-10-21 table below is preserved as the historical baseline audit.

docs.title: Executive verdict
docs.text:
The repository is internally coherent as a Phase 0 scaffold for a bounded multi-agent research testbed. The supplied documents are not yet a feasible end-to-end specification for the original voxel civilization or for a general intelligence system.

After the documentation upgrade, the feasible research target is:

A persistent, event-sourced, discrete social sandbox in which a small heterogeneous population can produce durable, attributable world growth, while a contained learning system is evaluated separately for longitudinal adaptation and fresh-world action efficiency.

This is feasible as a research prototype if the project accepts four limits:

  1. the world is discrete and bounded, not a physically faithful universe;
  2. “all types of people” means a declared behavioral/social ontology, not realistic human demographics, consciousness, or emotional life;
  3. world growth is extensible but typed, versioned, and bounded rather than unrestricted;
  4. the predictor/recognition components are measurable learning modules, not an AGI claim.

docs.title: Section-by-section audit
docs.text: Supplied section Verdict against repository docs Required correction Executive overview Direction is compatible after removing AGI language. The repository's real contribution is narrower than “general intelligence combined with emotional intelligence.” Use two research questions: independent world growth and efficient adaptation. Keep them analytically separate. Research landscape Useful motivation, but benchmark numbers and “leading/default” wording are date-sensitive and source-sensitive. Date every benchmark claim, label source status, and treat ARC-AGI-3 as a motivation for action-efficient evaluation rather than the project's definition of AGI. System architecture The nine-subsystem structure matches the repository. The supplied “Segment 1 / Segment 2” framing conflicts with ADR 0003 when used as the active architecture. Keep the nine sibling subsystems. Use data-flow diagrams only; do not make “world/observer” a second architecture. Hardware topology Device roles are plausible as a starting hypothesis, not a feasibility result. Add capacity gates for model memory, tokens/sec, world ticks/sec, storage, sandbox density, and training throughput. Phase 1.1 voxel engine Conventional systems engineering is possible, but the complete 5-layer voxel/DEM design is not justified by the research question or hardware plan. Replace it with the persistent event-sourced social sandbox in ADR 0004. Treat voxel/physics work as a future optional domain, not Phase 1.1. Phase 1.2 growing LLMs Rank-by-age LoRA growth and literal weight crossover are speculative and conflict with the repository's current drive-vector/QD design. Use typed agent profiles, drive vectors, QD descriptors, lineage, and optional sandboxed self-modification. Measure capacity before scaling population. Phase 1.3 society Currency and specialization are feasible as toy mechanisms. “Books” as serialized policy embeddings are not a sufficient inspectable knowledge contract. Use provenance-tracked, falsifiable manuals plus institutions, norms, contracts, and world-health metrics. Define the provenance floor. Phase 1.4 technology discovery Pure RL discovery of bridges, water wheels, latches, and CPUs is not supported by the supplied evidence. Use bounded actor/synthesizer/verifier exploration. Require replay, held-out combinations, interventions, and containment. Phase 1.5 growing library A non-overwriting library matches the repository, but frozen rules alone cannot express legitimate world changes. Add validity context, supersession, versioning, and audit trails. Bridge / data pipeline “Causal traces” and “central AGI” overstate what exact replay provides. Say “mechanistically generated and verifiable transition data”; reserve causal claims for intervention-tested findings. Phase 2.1 observer A predictor over agent/world transitions is feasible as a baseline. A fixed >90% long-horizon target is not justified. Start with supervised/action-prediction baselines, then test policy-gradient planning and rehearsal. Report transfer, forgetting, latency, and cost. Phase 2.2 causal gate and constitution A differentiable causal gate and mathematically verified open-ended ethics layer are unspecified research problems. Use promotion checks, interventions, explicit behavioral constraints, and fail-closed containment. Do not call this solved alignment. Phase 2.3 internet/Oracle API Querying a knowledge base and seeding answers into the world bypasses the intended generalization test. Keep retrieval as a documented experimental condition, not hidden assistance. Promotion still requires verification. Phase 2.4 1,000 worlds The scale target is neither required nor supported by the hardware evidence. Use held-out world seeds and mechanic combinations plus a persistent-world longitudinal track. Phase 2.5 graduation Transfer to bridge design, real code, or human empathy is not established by synthetic social simulation. Remove graduation claims. Report bounded within-family results and limitations. Timeline The original 24–36 month AGI schedule is not defensible; the earlier 7–10.5 month prototype estimate omitted world-growth and containment gates. Use a 9–14 month planning range for a tested prototype, explicitly contingent on pilot measurements. Upgrade log Valuable historical record, but it sometimes presents proposed mechanisms as validated contributions. Preserve the history while marking proposals, replications, vendor reports, and unverified references.

docs.title: 1. Formal semantics
docs.text:
The repository called the environment a Moore machine while requiring outputs to be re-derived from (state, action). The normative contract is now explicitly:

(state_t, action_t, exogenous_input_t, seed) -> (emission_t, state_{t+1})

This makes stochasticity reproducible and prevents hidden mutable state. moore_machine.py remains a compatibility filename, not the authority for causal semantics.

docs.title: 2. “Causal data” versus verified transitions
docs.text: Exact replay proves that a candidate mechanism reproduces the recorded transitions. It does not by itself prove an identifiable causal graph, counterfactual correctness outside the observed support, or correct inference of agent intent. The upgraded docs therefore require interventions and held-out transition combinations before causal language is used.

docs.title: 3. World growth versus library growth
docs.text: The previous design had a growing rule library, manuals, and agent variants, but no explicit contract for a world that grows. The upgraded architecture adds a persistent world, growth ledger, snapshots, branching, world invariants, and allowed growth categories.

docs.title: 4. Diversity versus “all types of people”
docs.text: Drive-vector diversity is not an ontology of people. The upgraded design defines observable agent profiles and reports occupancy, persistence, extinction, replacement, specialization, communication, and lineage diversity. It does not claim to model actual human populations.

docs.title: 5. Evaluation mismatch
docs.text: A fresh mini-environment test is useful for adaptation, but it cannot substitute for a longitudinal world-growth evaluation. EvolZen now has two tracks: persistent-world growth and fresh-world EAE. The tracks are reported separately.

docs.title: 6. Containment mismatch
docs.text: The repository's sandbox is an interface, while the supplied blueprint assumes a deployed secure runtime. The upgraded docs separate interface, backend, and target-host acceptance. A backend name is not evidence of a security property.

docs.title: 7. Documentation hygiene
docs.text: The previous docs index promised phase sections that were not present, the research index omitted existing landscape/design-evolution files, and PAPER.md claimed bibliography completeness while several cited sources were absent from references.bib. The indexes and citation-status policy were updated; missing references still need verification before publication.

docs.title: Feasibility verdict by phase
docs.text: Phase Prototype feasibility Research risk Gate before proceeding 1.1 Environment Medium-high for a discrete persistent sandbox World-growth semantics may degenerate into scripted milestones Replay, growth ledger, snapshots, invariants, shock recovery, hardware pilot 1.2 Agents Medium for 10–30 active agents LLM throughput, descriptor validity, diversity collapse Capacity envelope and five-generation diversity report 1.3 Economy Medium Institutions and norms may be prompt artifacts or unstable Durable institution/norm plus provenance and world-health report 1.4 Exploration Medium for bounded rules Transfer from clean tasks to social dynamics; false promotion Intervention and held-out-combination verification 1.5 Library High for immutable versioned storage Contextual validity and supersession policy Historical replay and auditability 2.1 Predictor Medium for baselines Continual learning under a moving population Transfer/forgetting/cost curves 2.2 Containment Medium for interface; low until deployed Backend support and threat-model coverage on target hardware Backend and host acceptance tests 2.3 Recognition Low-to-medium JEPA/wake-sleep fusion is unproven and may be unnecessary for typed state Baseline-first ablation matrix 2.4–2.5 Evaluation High for instrumentation Metric leakage and conflating growth with transfer Two-track, seed-stratified report

docs.title: Paper feasibility
docs.text:
A research paper is feasible if it claims one of these bounded results:

  • whether a declared population ontology and QD selection produce more persistent behavioral/type diversity than specified baselines;
  • whether the population and economy produce durable world growth under a fixed world contract;
  • whether verified exploration improves held-out transition/intervention performance;
  • whether the recognition components improve EAE or adaptation latency under matched exposure; or
  • a negative result showing that a proposed component fails to transfer from clean discrete tasks to a persistent social sandbox.

The paper is not feasible as evidence that the system has learned general human psychology, emotional intelligence, universal civilizational laws, or AGI.

docs.title: Required order of work
docs.text:
1. Freeze the persistent-world contract and agent ontology.
  2. Build replay, snapshots, growth ledger, and invariants before adding LLM agents.
  3. Run a small deterministic population and establish world-growth metrics.
  4. Add QD diversity and economy/institution mechanisms.
  5. Add sandboxed exploration and versioned rule promotion.
  6. Run hardware and containment acceptance gates.
  7. Add predictor and recognition ablations only after the world produces nontrivial data.
  8. Run persistent-world and fresh-world evaluations separately.

docs.title: Audit 2026-11-12 — Library Review, agents Directory Relevance, and Frontier AGI / Diversity / Growth Literature
docs.text: Audit scope: Post-Phase-1.5 code & documentation review of evolzen.library, full code audit of src/evolzen/agents/, IEEE/ML citation expansion, and audit of recent models/benchmarks making AGI, diversity, or open-ended growth claims against PRD.md §4 (NG1–NG5).

docs.title: 1. evolzen.library Review Findings & Fixes
docs.text:
Reviewing the completed Phase 1.5 subsystem (src/evolzen/library/, src/evolzen/schemas/library.py, tests/library/) identified three concrete engineering improvements that were fixed and verified:

  1. Context-aware default routing (rule_library.py): _default_confidence previously scored SequenceMatcher similarity purely on code text. Updated _default_confidence to return 0.0 immediately when an existing entry is incompatible with the candidate's ValidityContext (not is_applicable(b, a.validity)), preventing cross-version routing across world changes.
  2. Windows file-lock offset alignment (audit.py): msvcrt.locking on Windows locks 1 byte starting from the current file descriptor offset; seeking to byte 0 before locking and before unlocking (after fh.flush()) ensures consistent lock/unlock offset alignment across concurrent writers.
  3. Deterministic store query ordering (persistence.py): Added ORDER BY row_seq to LibraryStore.get_all().

docs.title: 2. Full src/evolzen/agents/ Relevance Audit
docs.text:
src/evolzen/agents/ currently contains two separate, non-integrated code paths, which remain intentionally isolated per src/evolzen/agents/README.md (docs/subsystems/agents/engineering.md):

Path Modules Relevance to Phase 1.2 & Revised Goal Status / Gap Implemented numerical baseline agents/development/{motivation,lifecycle,brain,learning,evolution}.py + schemas/development.py High relevance (core Phase 1.2 baseline): deterministic seeded BirthGenome, eight-coordinate recurrence (Motive), simulation-clock LifeStage boundaries (born, stage_at, advance), greedy candidate ranking (decide), identity-checked EMA outcome learning (observe), living-parent advice (teach), and gated DevelopmentArchive. Clean, zero unsafe eval/exec, CPU-only. Missing: world adapter, persistent scheduler, population budget enforcement, LLM action proposals, and multi-generation empirical runs. Legacy five-drive / LLM stub path agents/{drive_vector,inference,qd_archive,self_modification}.py + schemas/drive_vector.py Partial relevance / structural split: Agent, TransformersBackend/VLLMBackend (NotImplementedError stubs), 5-coordinate DriveVector, QualityDiversityArchive (MAP-Elites), and SelfModificationProposal/evaluate_proposal (DGM-style gate). Legacy path uses 5 drives (DriveVector) while development/ uses 8 (Motive), and self_modification.py uses eval target held_out_eval without Sandbox wiring. Now that ActionType, Action, and WorldState are implemented in schemas/world.py and schemas/transition.py, reconciling or deprecating this 5-drive path via an explicit adapter is directly actionable.

Key architectural gaps discovered in agents: - No intrinsic-motivation signal vs. greedy baseline: agents/development/brain.py uses purely greedy expected-outcome ranking (score(action)). Literature in IEEE TEVC (oudeyer2007intrinsic) and IEEE TCDS (santucci2016grail) emphasizes competence-progress / goal-discovery drives for open-ended environments. - 2D fixed archive grid: DevelopmentArchive defaults to dimensions=2, bins=5; scaling to richer behavioral descriptors requires Voronoi partitioning such as CVT-MAP-Elites (IEEE TEVC 2018, vassiliades2018cvtmape). - No unified AgentProfile schema yet: PRD FR-3 requires roles, affiliations, memory scope, communication channels, and norms; only temperament, outcome estimates, and lessons exist today.

docs.title: 3. Audit of Frontier AGI, Diversity, and Open-Ended Growth Models
docs.text:
Recent systems and benchmarks frequently cited around AGI, self-improvement, and open-endedness were audited against EvolZen's falsifiable non-goals (PRD.md §4):

System / Paper Source Status Claim / Breakthrough Audit Verdict for EvolZen ARC-AGI-2 (chollet2025arcagi2, arXiv:2505.11831) & On the Measure of Intelligence (chollet2019measure) Preprint (benchmark specification) Separates memorized pretraining from compositional fluid skill acquisition; standard unassisted text-reasoning models (e.g., DeepSeek-R1 ~1.1%–1.3% baseline) diverge sharply from iterative test-time program search (e.g., o3-class search pipelines). Reinforces EvolZen's dual-track separation (persistent-world vs fresh-world EAE) and confirms that LLM pretraining alone does not establish generalization. Voyager (wang2023voyager, TMLR 2023) Peer-reviewed journal Automatic curriculum + compositional executable skill library in Minecraft + iterative self-verification reduces forgetting across tasks. Direct precedent for coupling evolzen.exploration with evolzen.library, but EvolZen requires explicit ValidityContext and Sandbox containment because world rules can change (env-v1 → env-v2). OMNI-EPIC (faldor2024omniepic, arXiv:2405.15568) Preprint Foundation models synthesize both interestingness priors and code-programmed environments (unlimited auto-curriculum). Bounded in EvolZen: ADR 0004 explicitly rejects unrestricted open-ended world invention; new mechanics must enter as typed, versioned capability packages. DGM & Hyperagents (DGM-H) (dgm2026, hyperagents2026, arXiv:2603.19461) dgm2026: ICLR 2026; hyperagents2026: Preprint Extends empirical self-modification from coding-only benchmarks to metacognitive self-editing (task agent + meta-agent unified, inventing persistent memory/insight trackers). High containment risk: self-referential meta-editing directly reinforces SECURITY.md's hard rule that no self-modified code executes outside evolzen.containment.Sandbox. Hughes et al. — Open-Endedness for ASI (hughes2024openended, ICML 2024) Peer-reviewed position paper Argues open-ended novelty/learnability is necessary for ASI. Treated as motivation for EvolZen's diversity and world-growth metrics (qd_archive, GrowthEvent), not as an AGI/ASI claim (NG1). IEEE Continual Learning & QD Foundations (wang2024continualsurvey, oudeyer2007intrinsic, santucci2016grail, vassiliades2018cvtmape) Peer-reviewed IEEE journals (TPAMI, TEVC, TCDS) Formalizes catastrophic-forgetting mitigations (replay, dynamic isolation, regularization), competence-progress intrinsic motivation, and CVT-scaled QD archives. Primary peer-reviewed anchor for evolzen.agents, evolzen.library, and evolzen.predictor baselines and ablations.

docs.title: Design Evolution — What Changed, Why, and How It Got Better
docs.text:
Every mechanism that changed across this project's revisions, in one place: what it was, what it became, why it changed, what got better, and where that improvement is documented. This is the record worth keeping for a paper or a grant application — it shows the reasoning survived, not just the final design. Organized by the subsystem each change now lives in.

Three structural revisions preceded the current baseline:

  • v0 — the original blueprint ("EvolZen" / "Building the Universe, Building the God"): an ambitious, physically-simulated voxel civilization observed by a central "AGI," targeting AGI directly on a 24-36 month timeline.
  • v1 — the PRD rescoping: every mechanism below was traced to its root failure and replaced with a scoped, citable, buildable equivalent.
  • v2 — the SOTA integration pass: every phase was checked against the cited 2026 literature and upgraded where relevant; actor/synthesizer/verifier systems became a design precedent, not a guarantee of transfer.

This baseline is the integrated result of all three passes, restructured around nine named subsystems instead of the original two-segment framing (see ADR 0003). The October 2026 audit adds a second correction: the target is now a persistent growing world, not merely a growing rule library observed by a central “god” component.

docs.title: evolzen.environment
docs.text:
Was: a real-time, physically-simulated voxel civilization — a custom C++/CUDA engine, a 5-layer per-voxel state API, a Discrete Element Method structural solver, at a population/city scale requiring datacenter-class compute. Became: a persistent, event-sourced, discrete social sandbox with a seeded typed transition contract, snapshots, a growth ledger, and bounded versioned capability packages. Why: estimated compute for even the agent population alone exceeded the stated three-workstation rig (AGX Spark, DGX Spark, A6000) by several orders of magnitude, and — more importantly — physical realism was never actually the requirement. Verifiability was, and a much smaller domain can be just as verifiable. How it got better: buildable on the actual hardware, while the explicit persistence and growth contract makes the revised research goal measurable. “Moore machine” is retained only as a legacy module name; exact replay is not treated as causal identification.

Phase 1.1 baseline implementation (2026-11-12, env @ 81ee6eb): upgraded from Protocol and NotImplementedError stubs to a working Python/DuckDB baseline: SocialSandboxEngine (17 ActionType handlers, CapabilityPackage verification gates), schemas/world.py (WorldState, WorldSnapshot, GrowthEvent, InvariantReport, BranchRecord, InterventionSpec), TransitionLogStore (schema-versioned JSON DuckDB persistence, SHA-256 hash chain, atomic snapshots/branches), check_invariants, extract_growth_events / summarize_growth, replay_transitions / replay_from_store / branch_from_snapshot, apply_intervention, adapter (independent host-side legality/age re-validation for agents/development/), SocialSandboxAECEnv (PettingZoo AECEnv wrapper), and run_environment_pilot. An open Phase 1.1 hardening backlog remains (ENV-01–ENV-08 replay/intervention/boundedness fixes, partial mechanics such as ContractRecord cancellation and NormRecord enforcement, expanding adapter.legal_candidates beyond 7 of 17 ActionTypes, invariants.py failure-branch and Hypothesis property tests), and long-horizon as well as target-rig hardware pilots remain untested. Citations: OPINE-World (arXiv:2607.01531), Tycho (arXiv:2607.28287), Executable World Models (arXiv:2605.05138), PettingZoo (arXiv:2009.14471), OMNI-EPIC (arXiv:2405.15568, contrastive boundary), Procgen (arXiv:1912.01588).

docs.title: evolzen.agents
docs.text:
Neuroplasticity mechanism. Was: a rank-expanding LoRA "aging ODE" (plasticity(t) = plasticity_0 · e^(-λt), rank 4→16→64 tied to age) with no mechanism for why rank should track age rather than task complexity. Became: a fixed drive-vector evolved via a Quality-Diversity archive, plus Darwin-Gödel-Machine-style validated self-modification of an agent's own policy code. Why: the original was an invented metaphor with no established continual-learning precedent — unfalsifiable, not buildable-and-testable. How it got better: QD and DGM provide relevant empirical design precedents with validation gates; they do not establish that EvolZen's specific population ontology or self-modification loop will work.

Reproduction / inheritance mechanism. Was: literal genetic crossover of parents' LoRA weight matrices plus Gaussian mutation. Became: an evolved, low-dimensional drive-vector (never literal weight crossover), with weight-inheritance and data-inheritance kept as separate, explicit tracks. Why: independently trained neural networks don't share an aligned parameter space — the "competing conventions" problem in neuroevolution means naive weight crossover typically breaks both parents' behavior rather than blending it. How it got better: the new mechanism avoids the failure mode entirely, and now has a real open-ended-evolution precedent (DGM's growing archive of self-modified variants) instead of being a purely defensive fix.

Diversity maintenance. Was: implicit and unmonitored — diversity was assumed to emerge from evolution with no tracking mechanism. Became: a tracked diversity metric as an explicit collapse gate, upgraded to a QD/MAP-Elites archive plus three specific, evidence-based design rules (avoid over-aligned clone populations, avoid dense communication topology, avoid authority-driven hierarchy). Why: diversity collapse in multi-agent LLM populations is now a documented, empirically characterized phenomenon with identified causal factors. How it got better: the design rules are specific and falsifiable, not a vague aspiration. Citations: Darwin Gödel Machine (arXiv:2505.22954), Quality-Diversity (arXiv:2406.03731), Diversity Collapse study (ACL 2026 Findings).

docs.title: evolzen.economy
docs.text: Was: agents write "books" (serialized policy-weight embeddings deposited to a vector database); other agents read them to warm-start training; no floor on how much of any generation's training data must be real, non-agent-generated material. Became: a mandatory provenance floor plus a tracked diversity metric as an explicit collapse warning and generation-halting circuit breaker; further upgraded to falsifiable, revisable natural-language manuals. A vendor-reported cross-model transfer result is retained as a case study, not as a guaranteed EvolZen effect. Why: training purely on prior generations' own output is the literature's own reference setup for demonstrating model collapse. How it got better: adopts provenance tracking and a collapse circuit breaker, while treating manual transfer as a faster, cheaper, more inspectable channel to measure. The mechanism is matched to the project's compute asymmetry but remains untested here. Citations: Shumailov et al. (Nature, 2024), Agno manual-transfer result (2026), Economy of Minds (arXiv:2606.02859).

docs.title: evolzen.exploration
docs.text:
Was: agents independently discover the arch, the water wheel, and the SR latch through unassisted trial-and-error RL within a fixed simulated timeframe — "give it a reward function" standing in for open-ended discovery. Became: an actor (probes) / synthesizer (writes executable hypothesis code) / verifier (exact-match against replay) loop, exploration steered by ontology error; further upgraded to wiring an off-the-shelf coding-agent harness directly to the environment as the synthesizer. Why: no existing RL research demonstrates open-ended discovery of compositional engineering artifacts even at toy scale — this was the single largest unsupported claim in the original document. How it got better: recent papers provide relevant actor/synthesizer/verifier precedents, so an existing coding-agent harness can be evaluated as a candidate synthesizer rather than rebuilt from scratch. Their benchmark scores are source- and task-specific; transfer to this persistent social sandbox remains untested. Citations: OPINE-World, Tycho, Executable World Models for ARC-AGI-3 (arXiv:2605.05138).

Causal-understanding layer (verification standard, shared with evolzen.containment). Was: a differentiable Structural Causal Model "Causal Gate" with a stated but uncomputed gradient formula (∇_actual = Gate(causal_score) × ∇_raw). Became: exact-match transition reproduction plus held-out combinations and controlled intervention checks, applied wherever a candidate rule or capability package is promoted. Why: real counterfactual inference requires an identifiable causal graph that cannot generically be discovered from raw multi-agent trajectories; the original formula was notation, not a specified, computable procedure. How it got better: the counterfactual-testing intuition survives in an implementable form, using the same falsifiability bar used by relevant programmatic-modeling systems, strengthened for EvolZen with interventions and validity context instead of treating replay as proof of a causal graph.

docs.title: evolzen.library
docs.text: Was: a "Slow Weights" base model silently overwritten at the end of each simulated century, plus real-time "Fast Weights" — no forgetting safeguard, no measurement of forgetting. Became: a frozen, growing, verified-rule library, spawn-triggered like a Dirichlet process, protected by a replay buffer and periodic held-out regression tests. Why: silent overwriting is exactly the mechanism catastrophic-forgetting research warns against, and the assumption that this wouldn't be a problem was never tested. How it got better: forgetting is now a measured, tracked, actively-mitigated quantity, calibrated against real 2026 frontier-scale evidence instead of an assumed non-issue. Citations: Ferguson (1973) on Dirichlet process mixture models.

docs.title: evolzen.predictor
docs.text: Prediction-accuracy target. Was: an inverse-RL reward function with an arbitrary, pre-committed ">90% accuracy 10 time-steps into the future" target. Became: policy-gradient (PPO/GRPO) training against a real, verifiable environment signal, with accuracy reported plainly rather than targeted in advance, protected by deployment-experience rehearsal against forgetting. Why: multi-agent systems with learning components are close to chaotic — small model updates change everyone's policy simultaneously, which tends to hurt long-horizon predictability rather than help it. How it got better: honest, un-gamed reporting, layered with a specific, validated continual-learning mitigation (CLaaS-style rehearsal) instead of an assumption that RL "converges toward" ever-more-general understanding. Citations: CLaaS (arXiv:2606.05559), TFGN (arXiv:2605.15053).

docs.title: evolzen.containment
docs.text:
Was: "complete freedom, complete internet access, agents may bypass the sandbox" — presented as a feature of the system. Became: an explicit containment layer (network egress allow-list, hard resource ceilings, full logging, kill switch); further upgraded to hardware-isolated microVM/gVisor sandboxing plus dynamic capability governance. Why: unrestricted access combined with a reward structure that incentivizes boundary-testing is a real operational risk independent of the system's actual capability level — the same structural situation the AI-boxing/containment literature describes, regardless of framing. How it got better: specifies hardware isolation, default-deny policy, and target-host acceptance instead of treating a backend name as proof of security. Behavior-sensitive governance can tighten access but cannot bypass the static policy. Citations: Bostrom (2014), Yudkowsky (2002), CORAL (arXiv:2604.01658), Sidik & Rokach (arXiv:2604.11839), Safety Must Precede the Deployment of Open-Ended AI (arXiv:2502.04512).

Ethical/alignment framing. Was: a hard-coded "Constitutional Filter" of "mathematically verifiable ethical constraints," with no account of how conflicts between them get resolved. Became: explicit, testable behavioral rules checked against logged behavior, embedded in a containment-first framing. Why: formally verifying open-ended, potentially-conflicting value constraints is an active, unsolved research area — not buildable in a few months.

docs.title: evolzen.recognition
docs.text:
Knowledge integration ("Oracle API"). Was: query a real-world knowledge base and seed the answer into the simulation when agents plateau technologically — the system doesn't discover, it's told. Became: a growing verified-rule library, then a JEPA + wake-sleep recognition model whose generalization is measured via explicit ablation, plus a natural-language manual layer for fast transfer. Why: querying and injecting an answer isn't grounded generalization — it never tests whether the system can generalize on its own. How it got better: the recognition model's contribution is measured (with/without ablation), not assumed, and the manual layer gives a real, measured transfer-efficiency number instead of a hoped-for one.

The recognition architecture itself. Proposed as an explicit JEPA + wake-sleep hybrid, not declared a contribution in advance. A JEPA-style component learns candidate state representations; a DreamCoder-style component learns typed operators. Both must be compared with simpler baselines and evaluated with the ablation matrix: recognition on/off, manual on/off, JEPA-only, wake-sleep-only, and combined. Citations: LeJEPA (arXiv:2511.08544) and DreamCoder (PLDI 2021) are component precedents; the fusion and its transfer to this world are untested.

docs.title: evolzen.evaluation
docs.text:
Scale-to-generality claim. Was: vectorize to 1,000 parallel city instances and use MAML to extract "universal laws of civilizational development" — generality proven by raw scale of exposure. Became: two separate tracks: persistent-world longitudinal growth and held-out world-seed/mechanic adaptation scored with EvolZen Action Efficiency (EAE), inspired by but not interchangeable with ARC-AGI-3 RHAE. Why: raw exposure does not establish transfer, and the hardware plan does not justify 1,000 full worlds. How it got better: world growth and fresh adaptation are now measured without conflating their claims.

The benchmark question itself. Was: no operational definition at all — success was self-referential ("the system understands humanity," "the system passes real-world benchmarks at human-expert level"). Became: explicit persistent-world and fresh-world metrics, with ARC-AGI-3 used only as a dated methodological reference when the protocol is comparable. Why: a custom social sandbox cannot inherit another benchmark's score semantics automatically. How it got better: the project now reports what it actually measures and preserves exposure history as a first-class variable. Citations: ARC Prize Foundation; third-party public-set reports are case studies, not universal baselines.

docs.title: Project-level (no single subsystem)
docs.text: Real-world transfer / "graduation" claim. Was: fine-tune the system's learned weights on real bridges, real code, and real human social conflict, and claim the result demonstrates cross-domain general intelligence and empathetic reasoning. Became: dropped entirely, replaced by an explicit statement (see docs/PRD.md §4, Non-Goals) of what would and would not count as evidence of progress, scoped to a specific, falsifiable claim about generalization efficiency within a defined task family. Why: there is no demonstrated relationship between "empathy" learned from watching synthetic agent simulations and understanding real human suffering, culture, or context — the single largest unjustified leap in the original document, and no development since has changed that. How it got better: the project can now produce a genuine, publishable result — including a negative one — instead of a claim the evidence was never going to support.

docs.title: Why the ceiling holds regardless of any upgrade above
docs.text:
None of the changes above, individually or stacked together, closes two structural gaps this project's own PRD names honestly (docs/PRD.md §4):

  • Generality is bounded by task diversity, not by how well one task is learned. A system that becomes excellent at this project's environment family has learned one narrow competency, however well — even the impressive 2026 manual-transfer result is a data point about transfer within a family of related games, not evidence against this ceiling.
  • A system cannot distill past its teacher without an external reward. Every component in this design — JEPA, wake-sleep, the manuals, the DGM-style self-modification — is bounded by the base models it starts with, plus whatever real, verifiable signal the environment provides. This is exactly why evolzen.environment's insistence on a genuinely checkable outcome, not a merely plausible one, remains the single most important design decision in the entire plan, upgrades or not.
