Official implementation documentation inspected on the same date: gVisor's What is gVisor? page (gvisor.dev/docs/) describes a userspace application kernel, explicitly not an ordinary VM; Firecracker's project page (firecracker-microvm.github.io) describes KVM-backed microVMs. These clarify isolation terminology, not the security of an untested EvolZen deployment.

docs.title: Explicitly unsupported hypotheses
docs.text:
• Seven sins plus Null span all personality or emotional dimensions.
  • A randomized equation is equivalent to subjective thought or human intention.
  • Age causes competence, or an exponential plasticity curve reflects real development.
  • More generations guarantee cultural accumulation.
  • Local numerical learning is equivalent to continual neural training.
  • A public/private leaderboard gap is a controlled estimate of the benefit of manuals.

These assertions are not adopted. The documents instead specify observable behavior, matched comparisons and clear implementation status. The equation, budgets, stage thresholds, action ranking, advice weights and EMA updates are EvolZen design decisions, empirically untested.

docs.title: Individual training, cultural transfer and population evolution
1. Implemented baseline loop
docs.text:
The baseline is pure numerical policy adaptation, not neural self-training:

  1. Host provides permitted observations, normalized context and bounded candidate actions.
  2. decide updates eight activations, computes ratios, ranks legal candidates, and stores one pending decision with agent ID, sequence, world tick, outcome prediction and utility.
  3. The environment executes the chosen action under independent constraints.
  4. The trusted verifier produces an Outcome matching agent/sequence/action and a transition evidence ID. Text generated by the agent is not an outcome oracle.
  5. observe consumes the matching pending receipt once and updates the context/skill estimate.
  6. The host persists both decision and outcome; a later decision can change because of learning.

For each component of an existing outcome estimate:

estimate_new = (1 - alpha) * estimate_old + alpha * observed_reward

The first observation initializes the estimate. Rewards are eight fixed, independently measured world-outcome features in [-1,1]. This learns consequences; only action selection uses current motivation ratios. It avoids replaying old scalar rewards under a changed preference vector. There is no delayed-return credit assignment, counterfactual planner, gradient update, curiosity bonus or replay trainer in v1. Greedy selection may fail to explore useful alternatives.

Knowledge is keyed by (context_key, skill_key), which the host must version when dynamics or action parameters change. Memory, knowledge, lesson and candidate counts have separate limits. Knowledge eviction uses update recency, so forgetting is possible by design and must be measured. Samples count real accepted receipts, not repeated optimizer passes. Duplicate recent evidence is rejected; a global transition-ID deduplication store is still needed beyond the bounded window.

verified=True and assessment flags are caller contracts, not cryptographic proof. Do not expose receipt construction or observe directly as model-callable tools. Serialized snapshots and restored flags must come from trusted host storage.

docs.title: 2. Teaching loop
docs.text:
teach(parent, child, context, skill, tick) requires recorded parentage, living maturity, a living learner, no pending actions, and personal parent evidence for the requested context/skill. It transfers a capped advice item with source evidence; the parent's evidence is unchanged. Repeated lessons replace the previous item for that teacher/context/skill rather than stacking authority. A child can revise an incorrect lesson through its own action feedback.

Future richer teaching adds demonstrations, manuals, questions and exercises. The teacher chooses what to demonstrate based on learning need and available budget; the learner must solve a different task instance. Teach incorrect but plausible material as a robustness control. Receiving a book, copying a sentence, or memorizing a demonstration is not measured skill acquisition.

docs.title: 3. Planned LLM self-training loop
docs.text:
Keep a shared frozen base and a versioned private adapter per learning agent where resources permit:

collect trusted trajectories -> split by episode/world/lineage
-> curate successes AND failures -> mix stratified historical replay
-> train candidate adapter offline -> independent validation + retention + safety
-> atomic checkpoint promotion or rejection -> resume next episode
  • Start with supervised action/outcome prediction and behavior cloning of verified trajectories.
  • Compare no-update, memory-only and adapter-update conditions at equal interaction/compute budgets.
  • Add RL only for a stated planning objective. PPO-style updates need policy-version bookkeeping; arbitrary old trajectories cannot silently become on-policy data.
  • Maintain scenario/rare-failure replay quotas. An external-data percentage is not a universal collapse cure; keep simulator, human-authored, model-generated and fantasy sources distinct.
  • Check age-specific curriculum performance and old-task retention before promotion. The model cannot change the evaluator, reward extraction, birth genome or safety policy to raise its score.
  • Do not expand LoRA rank merely because age increased. Capacity expansion is a separate proposal justified by measured benefit per additional memory/compute.
  • Curriculum advancement requires observed competence; aging without training is a control.

This adapter pipeline is planned, not implemented by observe. LoRA supports efficient adaptation, but does not itself guarantee continual-learning stability (Hu et al., 2021).

docs.title: 4. Population evolution
docs.text:
The new DevelopmentArchive implements bounded storage of externally evaluated mature snapshots in fixed behavior cells. Its descriptor is measured behavior—not the eight birth coefficients. A host assessment must match agent ID and validation-suite ID, be verified, pass safety, improve over its declared baseline, and stay within a retention-drop limit. Within a cell only a better score replaces the elite; a full archive refuses new cells. Rejected candidates remain the host's responsibility to log; no history is automatically persisted by the archive.

The scheduler still must implement selection and trials:

  1. Measure descriptor coverage, useful performance, cost and failure rates from completed runs.
  2. Consider validated agents for the archive using the same fixed evaluation suite/budgets.
  3. Select living mature parents with underrepresented behavioral niches and bounded lineage share.
  4. Check world resources, population cap and cooldown; create a new child with inherited equations.
  5. Run overlapping generations; parents can teach, but the child starts with no own evidence.
  6. Evaluate descendants on validation worlds; retain improved or useful diverse variants.
  7. Freeze the entire policy/archive for final unseen-world evaluation. Never use final test scores as repeated evolutionary fitness.

The implemented archive is a small MAP-Elites-inspired mechanism, not a claim of autonomous open-ended evolution. Self-modified executable policy code remains disabled until the real Sandbox backend exists. Numeric temperament sampling is not arbitrary code synthesis.

docs.title: 5. Growth versus reward hacking
docs.text: Do not define evolutionary fitness as “satisfies sins most strongly.” Use evaluator-owned world competence, adaptation and safety metrics. Report all eight outcome components, inactivity, resource consumption, population extinction and teaching cost. A high Null agent must not earn infinite positive reward for doing nothing; wait has a world-time/opportunity cost. Harmless low-activity agents can occupy valid diversity niches without dominating fitness by inaction.

docs.title: 6. Upgraded Learning & Convergence Roadmap (Proposed — ADR 0008)
docs.text:
The current EMA + greedy-argmax baseline has no regret bound, no non-convex Pareto coverage, one-step horizon, and assumes a stationary environment. Future milestones upgrade learning across three strictly ablated tiers (without claiming general intelligence per PRD.md §4):

  1. Tier 1 (Uncertainty + Non-Convex MORL): Track posterior variance in SkillEstimate for UCB (auer2002ucb1) / Thompson Sampling (russo2018thompson) exploration with sublinear regret, paired with Chebyshev scalarization (vanmoffaert2014morl) to cover non-convex multi-objective Pareto fronts.
  2. Tier 2 (Epistemic-Pragmatic Rollouts): Replace one-step ranking with Expected Free Energy (friston2015epistemic, parr2022activeinference) and multi-step latent world-model MPC (hafner2025dreamerv3, hansen2024tdmpc2) inside evolzen.predictor.planner.
  3. Tier 3 (Hierarchical Options + Multi-Agent Stabilization): Package verified RuleLibrary entries as temporal-abstraction options (I, pi, beta) (sutton1999options) and monitor multi-agent non-stationarity (busoniu2008marl) alongside CVT-MAP-Elites behavioral coverage.

docs.title: Birth and overlapping generations
docs.text:
born(id, seed, tick, config=..., parents=...) returns an immutable BrainSnapshot. A founder has no parents and generation zero. A descendant has one or two distinct living mature parents and generation 1 + max(parent generation). The new agent starts at age zero with no personal outcome estimates, memories or lessons. Its temperament is inherited numeric data; its knowledge is not. Birth does not kill or replace either parent.

One parent is permitted for simplified inheritance controls; two-parent reproduction is a second condition. Neither requires biological sex or sexual behavior. A population scheduler must enforce unique IDs, sufficient resources, maturity, cooldown, maximum live population and balanced lineage sampling before admitting a birth. The local born function validates lineage and maturity but cannot enforce global resource/population limits without the world.

docs.title: Stages and age
docs.text:
Default simulation thresholds are illustrative, configurable and not human years:

Age in world ticks Stage Intended curriculum (not auto-granted competence) 0–99 Child Observe, rest, simple resource use, supervised trial, receive lessons 100–299 Adolescent Wider tool practice, negotiation, independent experiments 300–999 Adult Resource allocation, eligible reproduction, teaching 1000–1499 Elder Continued learning, teaching, retrieval and skill consolidation 1500+ Dead No actions, learning, teaching or reproduction

Age is tick - born_at, never the number of LLM calls. All clocks are monotonic. Expiry is terminal; restore a pre-expiry branch only as an explicitly different experiment, not a revived agent in the same timeline. advance changes age without adding knowledge. It rejects a live pending action; terminal expiry cancels it and the host must record the cancellation. No hunger, illness, health-driven death or biological metabolism is implemented yet.

The domain supplies minimum action ages and rechecks legality during execution. Stage names are labels, not privileges. Safe tool access also requires capability checks and competence criteria. Learning rate is constant in the baseline so age and update budget can be separated experimentally. An age-dependent plasticity schedule is optional research, not a mandated exponential decay.

docs.title: What grows
docs.text:
1. Experience: outcomes seen in this lifetime, with evidence IDs.
  2. Knowledge: estimates, later manuals and evidence-linked episodic memories.
  3. Skills: held-out task performance, not an age-derived rank or birthday bonus.
  4. Planning: broader permitted action repertoire and, later, measured search competence.
  5. Culture: lessons transmitted while generations overlap.
  6. Population diversity: behavioral niches across descendants, measured separately from traits.

Base-model parameter count does not increase in v1. A future adapter expansion requires a capacity/compute budget, measured saturation, held-out benefit, retention checks and rollback. An old agent may keep learning; an inexperienced old agent must not be reported as an expert.

docs.title: Separate inheritance channels
docs.text:
Channel At birth During overlapping lives Status Temperament Numeric coefficient mixing plus bounded mutation Fixed within lifetime Implemented Personal evidence Empty Own verified outcomes Implemented numerical baseline Parental lessons Empty Evidence-linked advice from living mature parents Implemented World assets Host-defined transfer Trades/inheritance laws World integration pending Weights Shared base by default; no weight crossover Optional validated private adapter updates Planned Cultural manuals Explicit access policy; no omniscient global library Teach, contradict, revise Full manual integration pending

Teaching is non-destructive: parents retain what they teach. A lesson is context/version scoped and cannot certify a child's mastery. In v1 it influences only an unseen action's prior with a capped weight; the child's own experience takes precedence. Archived lessons may remain readable after a parent's death, but a new live teaching event cannot be emitted by a dead parent.

docs.title: Meaning of a “thinking child”
docs.text: A shared pretrained LLM already contains adult language and world knowledge. The child construct restricts local memory, permissions, curriculum and acquired game skills; it does not erase pretraining. A genuinely blank neural learner is a separate, much more expensive experiment. Report these two interpretations distinctly and include a pretrained-knowledge leakage probe.

docs.title: Motivation: a randomized, bounded birth equation
docs.text: Untested design hypothesis. Coordinate semantics and equations below are invented for EvolZen. They must be compared with simpler controls, not treated as laws of personality.

docs.title: Eight coordinates
docs.text:
All vectors use this order, recorded by Motive in schemas/development.py.

Coordinate Observable incentive Distinction and test Pride Reputation, status, mastery recognition Choose public credit versus identical private reward Greed Retained assets and future control of resources Save versus consume under equal survival need Lust Nonsexual attraction, affiliation and preferred experiences Social contact versus solitude; no sexualized child content Envy Relative disadvantage against a visible comparison group Hold own assets fixed while changing observed peer assets Gluttony Immediate consumption/satiation beyond baseline need Consume now versus retain resources; not identical to greed Wrath Response to perceived obstruction, threat or unfairness Protest/defend/repair under permitted action constraints Sloth Avoidance of effort and resource expenditure Lower-cost method of achieving the same end Null Disengagement/absence of goal pursuit Wait/abstain even where another zero-effort action exists

Low wrath does not mechanically imply kindness; high pride may encourage mastery or bluffing depending on opportunities and learned beliefs. Cooperation and care can emerge from multiple combinations but are not guaranteed or adequately modeled by these eight dimensions. Do not equate demographic identity with coefficient values. Future extensions need their own ablations.

docs.title: Inputs and normalization
docs.text:
The environment adapter produces an eight-element feature vector x_t in [-1, 1] with versioned feature definitions: status discrepancy, resource discrepancy, affiliation opportunity, relative disadvantage, consumption pressure, obstruction, fatigue, and disengagement opportunity. Each feature must come from the agent's permitted observations/internal needs, not evaluator secrets. Values outside the range, NaN, infinity and wrong dimensions are rejected, not clipped silently. Feature scaling is fixed on training data and logged with the scenario version.

For agent i, drive k at decision n:

a_k(n) = tanh(b_k + (1/8) sum_j W_kj x_j(n)
              + c_k age_fraction(n) + rho_k a_k(n-1))
p_k(n) = exp((a_k(n) - max(a(n))) / T) / sum_l exp((a_l(n) - max(a(n))) / T)

age_fraction = (world_tick - born_at) / lifespan for living agents. All eight ratios are nonnegative and sum to one; activations are bounded [-1, 1]. A ratio is relative priority, not a probability that the agent will commit a particular act. Null is an explicit competing coordinate; it is not 1 - sum(other unnormalized values).

Founder coefficients are sampled with a local seeded generator: b,c uniform [-0.5,0.5], W uniform [-1,1], rho uniform [0,0.5], T=1. Coefficients are frozen birth data. Seeds and full coefficients are persisted; seed alone is not a portable serialization format. Inheritance averages aligned numerical coefficients plus bounded uniform mutation; rho stays [0,1]. T remains the parent mean. No equations are strings, and no eval or generated Python is used.

The equation advances once per decision, not every empty world tick. This is a simple recurrence, not a continuous-time ODE. Compare decision-rate-matched agents to avoid confounding momentum with action frequency. Periodicity, cross-drive recurrence, homeostatic feedback and learned equations are future variants, not features of v1.

docs.title: From preferences to choices
docs.text:
Each domain candidate has an immutable action ID, context key, skill key, eight predicted outcome values, cost, minimum age and domain permission flag. Context/skill keys must distinguish materially different action parameters and world-rule versions.

score(action) = sum_k p_k * expected_outcome_k(action) - cost(action)

Expected outcomes are the agent's own empirical estimate when available. Otherwise they are the supplied candidate prediction, blended with at most 25% parental advice (10% default). Own experience overrides parental advice. The highest score wins; action ID breaks ties, making candidate ordering irrelevant. Candidate counts are bounded. If no candidate is legal the call fails; the host must supply an explicit legal wait action when needed.

docs.title: Theoretical grounding & formal classification
docs.text:
While the seven-sins-plus-Null names and $8 \times 8$ tendency matrix $W_{kj}$ are untested EvolZen design choices, their mathematical form maps directly onto three established frameworks in IEEE and ML literature:

  1. Homeostatic Drive Modulation (Keramati & Gutkin, eLife 2014, keramati2014homeostatic): The context vector $x_t \in [-1, 1]^8$ encodes discrepancies (resource deficit, status gap, consumption pressure, fatigue). Modulating drive activations $a_k(n)$ from internal and environmental deviations functions as a bounded homeostatic weighting mechanism rather than a claim about human emotion.
  2. Multi-Objective Linear Scalarization (Hayes et al., AAMAS 2022, hayes2022morl): Evaluating score(action) = sum_k p_k * expected_outcome_k(action) - cost(action) is mathematically MORL linear scalarization using dynamic preference weights $p_k(n)$ over an 8-dimensional reward vector. By MORL theory, linear scalarization can only recover policies on the convex hull of the Pareto front; whenever trade-offs (e.g., safety vs. immediate consumption) are non-convex, future variants must ablate non-linear (Chebyshev) utility instead of assuming linear weights suffice.
  3. Priority Ratios vs. Stochastic Policy Operators (Asadi & Littman, ICML 2017, asadi2017mellowmax): drive_step uses Boltzmann softmax solely to normalize $a_k(n)$ into positive priority weights $p_k(n)$, while decide uses deterministic argmax (ranked[0]). If future versions convert action scores into stochastic exploration policies, standard Boltzmann softmax can suffer from non-contraction/multiple fixed points under value iteration; the Mellowmax operator provides a provably non-expansive alternative to test against greedy selection and $\epsilon$-greedy.

This baseline is greedy and does not implement curiosity, planning or autonomous exploration (compare Merrick, IEEE TAMD 2010, merrick2010valuesystems; Colas et al., JAIR 2022, colas2022autotelic). A controlled exploration schedule, intrinsic competence-progress term, or LLM proposal distribution must be added as a separately measured condition. Predicted utility is not factual truth; observed outcome updates are how the baseline corrects a mistaken preference-to-action expectation.

docs.title: Preferences are not permissions
docs.text:
Candidate masks are only an initial host-provided filter. The environment independently checks action legality and lifecycle permissions on execution. A high wrath or greed ratio cannot grant network access, change the reward evaluator, override containment, or alter another agent's memory. Hard constraints sit outside utility maximization; violations cannot be traded for reward.

For future LLM reasoning, use ratios as structured goal-selection and memory-retrieval inputs, then compare against ranking-only. Do not claim that a prompt changes internal neural reasoning without controlled evidence. Log concise goal IDs, candidates, scores and evidence—not hidden chain-of-thought.

docs.title: Containment integration
docs.text:
Authority: Phase 2.2 and repository-root SECURITY.md. Source package: src/evolzen/containment/.

No motivational ratio can grant a capability. Numeric coefficients are data under a fixed interpreter; self-modified source code is a different risk and must run through Sandbox. The developmental core performs no action execution, filesystem writes, model loading or network access. Feedback and assessment flags are host-only inputs, not authenticated proofs. A deployed isolation backend is still required before enabling generated code; a Python interface or restricted namespace is not that backend.

docs.title: Economy integration
docs.text:
Authority: Phase 1.3. Source package: src/evolzen/economy/.

Own resource transfer, teaching time costs, institutions, manuals and data provenance. Greed versus gluttony requires a distinction between retaining and consuming assets; envy uses permitted relative information, not hidden balances. Teaching is a transfer of evidence-linked advice, not an automatic grant of resources or competence. Full manuals-to-lessons integration is pending; the developmental baseline transfers only numerical context/skill estimates. Do not treat synthetic family knowledge as externally sourced data.

Implemented Phase 1.3 components: - Market & OrderBook (market.py): Integer currency balances, Hayekian dynamic scarcity pricing (quote_price), continuous double auction order matching with institutional fee withholding, ActionType.TRADE action construction, and settle_in_world preserving exact conservation invariants; - ManualStore (manuals.py): Falsifiable natural-language manuals, revision lineages, automated real-data provenance floor calculations (calculate_real_fraction), generation corpus gating (verify_generation_corpus), and forward knowledge transfer measurement (measure_knowledge_transfer); - EconomicMetrics (metrics.py): Gini inequality index, Herfindahl-Hirschman specialization index (HHI) and entropy, shock recovery resilience tracking, and macroscopic EconomicHealthReport evaluation; - Canonical schemas: ProvenanceSource and ProvenanceRecord in evolzen.schemas.manual.

Open downstream verification: - Empirical multi-generation benchmarks testing specialization emergence, manual revisions under induced falsification, and macro-resilience across 5 generations on target DGX/AGX hardware remain untested; success metrics are unmeasured.

docs.title: Environment integration
docs.text:
Authority: Phase 1.1. Source package: src/evolzen/environment/.

Own the world clock, agent observations, legal candidate generation, execution and outcome verification. Developmental agents consume eight normalized observable features and return a pending action ID; they do not mutate world state themselves. The environment must recheck age, resources, permissions and action parameters, then issue a matching trusted outcome receipt. Version context/skill keys with mechanics and meaningful action parameters.

Implemented Phase 1.1 core: - SocialSandboxEngine (engine.py) implementing Environment and PersistentEnvironment over (state_t, action_t, exogenous_input_t, seed) -> (emission_t, state_{t+1}), covering all 17 ActionTypes with verified CapabilityPackage gating (no arbitrary engine mutation); - canonical WorldState, WorldSnapshot, CapabilityPackage, GrowthEvent, WorldInvariant, InvariantReport, BranchRecord, and InterventionSpec contracts (evolzen.schemas.world); - check_invariants (invariants.py), extract_growth_events / summarize_growth (growth.py) across all five GrowthCategory buckets; - TransitionLogStore (evolzen.storage.transition_log, SCHEMA_VERSION = 1) for JSON-only DuckDB persistence, SHA-256 hash-chained transition appends, snapshots, growth events, and atomic save_snapshot_and_branch; - replay_transitions, replay_from_store, and branch_from_snapshot (replay.py); - apply_intervention (interventions.py); - adapter (observe_features, legal_candidates, action_from_candidate, execute_decision) for evolzen.agents.development, including independent host-side verification of Decision legality and minimum_age; - pettingzoo_env (SocialSandboxAECEnv) wrapping SocialSandboxEngine under PettingZoo's AECEnv contract (Discrete(10) with action_mask or typed Action); - run_environment_pilot (pilot.py) for local CPU throughput/storage benchmarking with snapshot_interval support.

Landed Stage 1 critical fixes: - replay_transitions passes current_state (not recorded.state) to engine.step, propagating state divergence accurately; - replay_from_store includes transitions up to up_to_tick, preserving same_tick=True multi-agent transitions; - apply_intervention supports sequence indexing (_set_nested_path) and reconciles ResourceAccounting.initial_currency; - _handle_spawn_offspring and _check_bounded_state evaluate capacity against active living agents rather than historical lineage records.

Landed Stage 2 host adapter full 17-action coverage: - adapter.legal_candidates and adapter.action_from_candidate cover all 17 ActionTypes (wait, gather, move, consume, craft, trade, propose_contract, fulfill_contract, found_institution, join_institution, contribute_institution, propose_norm, adopt_norm, assign_role, spawn_offspring, improve_location, register_capability); - Added cancel_contract:{cid} candidate generation and parsing for proposers of open contracts; - Host-side validation in execute_decision verifies legal candidate membership, dynamic permissions, and minimum age before stepping and returning verified Outcome receipts.

Landed Stage 3 operational mechanics: - Tool Durability & Fatigue Mitigation: Handlers _handle_gather and _handle_improve_location consume tool durability on work actions while halving physical fatigue accumulation; - Norm Compliance & Social Friction: _handle_gather evaluates conservation norms during common-pool harvesting, penalizing hypocrisy (-0.1 status/social reward) and community friction (-0.05 status/social reward) during resource scarcity (< 20% cap) while rewarding sustainable harvests (+0.02); - Institutional Trade Fee Withholding & Reserves: _handle_trade withholds contribution_rate fee on local trades directly to local_inst.currency_reserve while maintaining exact resource_conservation invariant; _handle_contribute_institution supports direct currency contributions; - Contract Cancellation & Expiration Sweep: Handlers support voluntary cancellation (cancel=True in _handle_fulfill_contract) and automatic expiration sweep (_expire_contracts) for stale open contracts exceeding TTL (100 ticks) or with deceased parties; - FR-2 Bounded Collections & Status: Enforced upper bounds on WorldAgentState.status ([0.0, 1.0]) across schemas, invariants, and engine handlers. Enforced capacity bounds (artifacts <= 512, contracts <= 256, institutions <= 64, norms <= 64, capabilities <= 64) in invariants.py and action rejection; - Exogenous Provenance: _apply_exogenous captures unhandled exogenous events (unhandled:<kind>) in applied_exog and records them in transition emissions (exogenous_applied).

Landed Stage 4 PettingZoo AECEnv upgrades & endogenous process attribution: - PettingZoo Macro-Shocks & Seeding: SocialSandboxAECEnv.step() accepts exogenous_input and deterministic seed kwargs, allowing RL and AEC callers to simulate macroeconomic shocks and seed schedules; - TransitionLogStore Hook: SocialSandboxAECEnv.__init__ accepts optional store: TransitionLogStore | None = None and automatically appends every executed transition with DuckDB hash-chain linkage; surfaces env.last_transition and env.store; - Expanded 16-Action Discrete Space: Expanded _act_space to Discrete(16) with full typed translation and action masks for trade, institution joining, contributions, norm proposals, norm adoptions, and reproduction alongside physical foraging/crafting; - Endogenous Process Growth Attribution: Added _expand_endogenous_ecology in engine.py, passively expanding carrying capacity by 1 for undisturbed flourishing ecosystems (shock_factor == 1.0, full resource capacity, next_tick % 50 == 0), activating the previously dormant GrowthAttribution.ENDOGENOUS_PROCESS emitter in growth.py.

Open Phase 1.1 hardening backlog (empirical metrics remain untested / unmeasured): - Untested validation & downstream scope: all 18 failure branches in invariants.py, Hypothesis property-based tests, empirical long-horizon Phase 1.1 runs, SocialSandboxAECEnv multi-agent learning integrations, LLM population scheduling (evolzen.agents, Phase 1.2), full market/manual provenance flows (evolzen.economy, Phase 1.3), sandboxed capability synthesis (evolzen.exploration, evolzen.containment, Phases 1.4/2.2), and target-rig hardware pilot measurements on DGX/AGX Spark. See agent engineering for the broader boundaries.

docs.title: Evaluation integration
docs.text:
Authority: Phases 2.4–2.5, system objectives, and developmental protocol. Source package: src/evolzen/evaluation/.

Keep world growth, individual learning, cultural transfer and population selection as distinct endpoints. Count teacher interactions, failed births, inactivity and discarded candidates in budgets. Split by family and world mechanics, not random ticks from a shared life. Evolution uses validation evidence; sealed final evaluations are never fitness feedback. Note: the existing rhae_scorer.py and minimal EvaluationReport helpers are early scaffolding slated for replacement by the per-episode EAE_B formula and full dual-track reporting contract.

docs.title: Exploration integration
docs.text:
Authority: Phase 1.4. Source package: src/evolzen/exploration/.

Agents' preference equations rank opportunities; they are not autonomous hypothesis synthesis. Keep empirical evidence separate from generated plans and reflection. Use declared observation budgets and intervention permissions. All generated rule/policy code executes only in Sandbox. The new greedy developmental core does not implement information-gain planning or curiosity; compare an exploration controller separately at equal budgets.

docs.title: Library Subsystem (evolzen.library)
docs.text: Authority: Phase 1.5 · Architecture: ARCHITECTURE.md §3.5 · API: evolzen.library

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
evolzen.library implements the Phase 1.5 growing, append-only verified-rule library (PRD FR-6, NFR-1). Verified rules and capability descriptions are persisted as immutable historical records with explicit provenance, validity contexts, verification evidence, supersession/deprecation metadata, a JSONL audit trail, and a held-out regression fixture bank.

[!NOTE] The spawn-or-route heuristic is motivated by Ferguson (1973) (Dirichlet process mixture analogy). This is a routing heuristic only, not a claim that the implementation is a Bayesian nonparametric model. Routing similarity is not proof of rule validity; code execution remains gated behind Phase 2.2 (evolzen.containment.Sandbox).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C["CandidateRule\n(evolzen.exploration)"] --> RL["RuleLibrary\n(rule_library.py)"]
    CP["CapabilityPackage\n(evolzen.schemas.world)"] --> RL
    RL -->|spawn / promote / supersede / deprecate / capability| LS["LibraryStore\n(persistence.py · DuckDB)"]
    RL -->|SPAWN / ROUTE / PROMOTE / SUPERSEDE / DEPRECATE| AL["AuditLog\n(audit.py · JSONL)"]
    RL -.->|context checks| V["validity.py\nis_applicable / needs_supersession"]
    RL <-->|export_to_world / import_from_world| WS["WorldState.capabilities\n(evolzen.environment)"]
    TL["TransitionLogStore\n(DuckDB transitions)"] -->|register_from_transition_store| RB["RegressionBank\n(regression_bank.py · DuckDB)"]
    RB -->|check_rule / check_all_active| RL
    LS --> S["evolzen.schemas.library\n(frozen Pydantic contracts)"]

docs.title: Module Responsibilities
docs.text: Module Role schemas/library.py Immutable (frozen=True, extra="forbid") Pydantic v2 contracts: RuleEntry, ValidityContext, VerificationEvidence, SupersessionLink, AuditEvent, RegressionResult, plus RuleStatus, ProvenanceClass, and AuditEventType. persistence.py LibraryStore — DuckDB append-only store with schema version guards (SCHEMA_VERSION = 1, schema_meta), per-call connections, and monotonically ordered row_seq sequences; persists both RuleEntry and CapabilityPackage records; retrieves latest state per entity via window functions without mutating prior rows. rule_library.py RuleLibrary — orchestrates spawn_if_novel (default difflib.SequenceMatcher routing or caller-supplied RoutingConfidenceFn), promote, supersede, deprecate, capability lifecycle (register_capability, get_capability, supersede_capability, export_capabilities_to_world, import_capabilities_from_world), and filtered querying (find_by_mechanic, find_by_world_version). validity.py Pure compatibility predicates (is_applicable, applicable_entries, needs_supersession, validate_supersession_reason) matching world_version, overlapping mechanic_keys, and intersecting seed_range. audit.py AuditLog & make_event — append-only JSONL writer with cross-platform file locking (msvcrt on Windows, fcntl on POSIX). regression_bank.py RegressionBank — stores pre-verified serialisable transition fixtures and records RegressionResult outcomes without executing RuleEntry.code; supports transition ingestion from Transition objects and TransitionLogStore.

docs.title: Append-Only Guarantee & Supersession Protocol
docs.text:
1. No physical updates or deletes: LibraryStore.update_status, LibraryStore.update_evidence, LibraryStore.update_capability_status, and RuleLibrary.supersede always insert a new row into rule_entries or capability_packages with a higher row_seq. Prior rows remain intact in DuckDB.
  2. Explicit supersession: Replacing a rule or capability when world mechanics or validity contexts change requires constructing a new entry (typically incrementing version while preserving family/package IDs) and providing a reason that is at least 10 non-whitespace characters.
  3. Separate provenance: ProvenanceClass (EXPLORATION_VERIFIED, HUMAN_AUTHORED, IMPORTED_EXTERNAL, UNKNOWN) keeps origin explicit rather than collapsing empirical estimates, advice, and verified rules into a single confidence scalar.
  4. Database schema version guard: LibraryStore initializes and checks the schema_meta table. Connecting to a database with a schema version greater than SCHEMA_VERSION raises a RuntimeError, preventing silent corruption from forward-incompatible schemas.

docs.title: Capability Package Persistence & World Integration
docs.text:
Phase 1.5 unifies rule discovery with Phase 1.1 environment capabilities (CapabilityPackage). Capabilities represent verified behavioral packages with action definitions, preconditions, and effects:

  • Storage Table: capability_packages table in DuckDB (row_seq, package_id, version, evidence_id, status, payload).
  • Store Operations:
  • append_capability(package, status): Append-only insertion of serialized capability JSON.
  • get_capability_by_id(package_id): Fetches the latest revision using windowed deduplication over row_seq.
  • get_active_capabilities(): Returns all latest capabilities with status == RuleStatus.ACTIVE.
  • list_capabilities_by_evidence(evidence_id): Filters capabilities by linked verification evidence ID.
  • update_capability_status(package_id, new_status): Appends an updated status row without modifying historical records.
  • World State Synchronization:
  • export_capabilities_to_world(world): Deep copies WorldState and merges active library capabilities into world.capabilities.
  • import_capabilities_from_world(world): Ingests verified capability packages from world.capabilities into LibraryStore.

docs.title: Transition Log Ingestion into Regression Bank
docs.text:
RegressionBank connects directly to recorded environment transitions to maintain empirical regression test fixtures:

  • register_from_transitions(rule_id, transitions, expected_emission_fn): Converts recorded Transition objects from Phase 1.1 into structured regression fixtures containing expected emission dictionaries (transition.emission.data), actions, states, and seeds.
  • register_from_transition_store(rule_id, store, run_id, up_to_tick, expected_emission_fn): Reads historical transition sequences from a DuckDB TransitionLogStore and registers them as regression test cases for the specified rule.
  • Security Boundary: Fixtures store plain serializable data and validate deterministic transition emissions without calling eval or exec on uncontained rule code.

docs.title: Audit Event Sequence
docs.text: Operation Audit Event Emitted Store Mutation spawn_if_novel (novel) AuditEventType.SPAWN Appends new RuleEntry (ACTIVE) spawn_if_novel (routed duplicate) AuditEventType.ROUTE None promote AuditEventType.PROMOTE Appends revision with updated VerificationEvidence supersede AuditEventType.SUPERSEDE Appends new RuleEntry, appends SUPERSEDED status row for old rule, appends SupersessionLink revert_supersession AuditEventType.REVERT Appends DEPRECATED row for replacement (if active) and ACTIVE row for old rule deprecate AuditEventType.DEPRECATE Appends DEPRECATED status row with deprecation_reason reject AuditEventType.REJECT None register_capability AuditEventType.PROMOTE or SPAWN Appends new CapabilityPackage (ACTIVE) supersede_capability AuditEventType.SUPERSEDE Appends SUPERSEDED status for old package, appends new CapabilityPackage RegressionBank.check_rule (with audit_log) AuditEventType.REGRESSION_CHECK Appends RegressionResult

docs.title: Regression Bank & Zero-Forgetting Metric
docs.text:
RegressionBank tracks serialisable transition fixtures (expected_emission vs actual_emission) and stores RegressionResult rows across rounds.

  • Security boundary: RegressionBank.check_rule never runs eval/exec on RuleEntry.code. Actual code replay belongs inside evolzen.containment.Sandbox (Phase 2.2) and evolzen.exploration.verifier (Phase 1.4).
  • Local vs. full validation: Fixture-based zero-forgetting across 3 rounds of additions is covered by tests/library/test_integration.py and tests/library/test_capability_integration.py, while live end-to-end replay against evolzen.exploration.verifier and evolzen.containment.Sandbox remains untested until Phases 1.4 and 2.2 are implemented.

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from evolzen.config import LibrarySettings, load_settings
from evolzen.library import AuditLog, LibraryStore, RegressionBank, RuleLibrary
from evolzen.schemas.world import CapabilityPackage

settings = load_settings(LibrarySettings, Path("configs/library.yaml"))
store = LibraryStore(settings.db_path)
audit = AuditLog(settings.audit_log_path)
library = RuleLibrary(store, audit, routing_threshold=settings.routing_confidence_threshold)
bank = RegressionBank(settings.db_path)

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• Default routing confidence uses difflib.SequenceMatcher on RuleEntry.code; semantic/embedding routing is deferred to evolzen.recognition (Phase 2.3).
  • RegressionBank.check_rule compares registered fixture emissions (expected_emission vs actual_emission) rather than executing untrusted rule code directly; sandboxed execution integration is pending Phase 2.2.

docs.title: Predictor integration
docs.text:
Authority: Phase 2.1. Source package: src/evolzen/predictor/.

Predict behavior under partial observation, distinguishing hidden birth temperament, changing activation, public actions and learned competence. Privileged access to drives is an oracle baseline, not a realistic intent-inference result. A synthetic intent label is not ground truth for real human intent. The agent's contextual EMA learner is separate from the system-level predictor and does not implement the existing planner's neural training methods.

docs.title: Recognition integration
docs.text:
Authority: Phase 2.3. Source package: src/evolzen/recognition/.

Learn a transferable hypothesis prior only after simpler representations and developmental baselines are evaluated. The eight-drive controller is not a JEPA encoder, emotional model or wake-sleep learner. Keep own experiences, parental advice and shared rules separately scoped. Test whether representation learning improves fresh-context transfer at matched exposure/cost; do not declare the architecture novel or effective before measuring it.
